title: 面对未知会恐惧，库洛创始人刘胜：我们做了很多难而正确的事
text:
做这个星球上最好的游戏
近日，广东在全网推出了《 思想耀岭南 》系列视频。其中在第15集，《思想耀岭南》制作团队专访了广州库洛科技有限公司创始人、董事长刘胜。
截止发稿时视频文字编译未获授权，如有侵权可联系删除
在采访中，刘胜回答了大量玩家和行业关注的问题，包括《鸣潮》的现状，库洛游戏海内外用户分布情况、中国游戏在国际上的竞争力，以及库洛的企业文化与愿景等等。
例如刘胜开篇就表示《鸣潮》开启全球巡回演唱会后的爆火现象超出自己的预期。而对于为何能取得成功的原因，他却非常朴素的认为:“本质上还是我们把游戏产品本身做好了。”
此外，他还提到目前库洛的海外活跃用户约占四成，主要分布在日本、韩国、欧美一些国家和东南亚一些国家；而国内活跃用户约占六成。
对于库洛本身的发展，刘胜坦然表示： 面对未知，面对一些比较难的事情，他们其实是会有恐惧的，但他们“ 做了很多难而正确的事” ，这其中包括技术迭代、自主发行、全球多平台运营等等，而“ 每件事情都难，但我觉得是正确的，它让我们的路越走越宽” 。
包括外界对库洛动作游戏做得好的评价，他也非常坦诚的称：他们其实没什么诀窍，就是比别人做得更细。当他们想让一个动作怎么看起来更和谐或更协调，他们就会反复调试和修改。
刘胜指出库洛倡导的就是“挑战即伟大”的企业文化，而他们的愿景和使命从未改变，就是做这个星球上最好的游戏。
值得一提的是，面对库洛到底是科技公司还是游戏公司，亦或者文化公司的问题，他强调库洛最核心的定位是游戏公司，但他们左手会跟科技握手、右手会跟文化握手。
以下是为广东发布、羊城晚报报道原文:
问：2025年12月，被誉为全球“游戏界奥斯卡”的TGA2025年度获奖名单揭晓，《鸣潮》斩获“玩家之声”奖项，这标志着中国游戏作品获得国际市场深度认可。2026年7月，《鸣潮》开启全球巡回演唱会。这种爆火现象是否超出您的预期？
答： 超出预期。达到这样一个受欢迎的程度，本质上还是我们把游戏产品本身做好了。我们最核心的一个目标就是让玩家更开心。游戏是一个比较复杂的综合体，玩家自己在家玩游戏、听游戏里的音乐，跟一万个人一起听喜欢的音乐，这种感受是非常不同的。
问：全球游戏赛道竞争激烈，做有国际竞争力的游戏，您有哪些心得体会？
答： 相对发达的区域，游戏的竞争也非常激烈，但游戏行业不存在真正意义上的垄断，只要是好的作品，就一定会被全球玩家看到。
问：库洛游戏的用户分布情况是怎样的？
答： 海外活跃用户约占四成，主要分布在日本、韩国、欧美一些国家和东南亚一些国家；国内活跃用户约占六成。
问：立足本土，放眼寰宇，国产游戏正在探索属于自己的国际化表达。在这方面，您有怎样的尝试和经验？
答： 做全球市场，一定会面临各个地方不同的文化特点和差异，首先你要保持自己的产品特色，在不同的版本中去尝试融入各种不同的文化符号，给玩家更多的选择权。
问：历经数十年产业沉淀，中国游戏积蓄了走向世界的底气。您如何评价中国游戏的国际竞争力？
答： 中国游戏在全世界是非常有竞争力的，中国有非常大的游戏人才规模。我们的游戏公司在“出海”方面有长足进步，以前是借船出海、买船出海，现在是自己造船出海。中国游戏的竞争力也从单点突破走向形成系统性优势。
问：追梦之路从无坦途，面对行业的重重未知，企业应该如何破局前行？
答： 面对未知，面对一些比较难的事情，我们其实是会有恐惧的，但我们过去做了很多难而正确的事情，做技术迭代、自主化的发行、全球多平台地运营游戏。每件事情都难，但我觉得是正确的，它让我们的路越走越宽。
我觉得游戏产业是一个数字化包装的文化产业，需要非常前沿的技术支持实现。现在大家会说库洛的动作游戏做得不错，这没有什么特别的诀窍，就是我们比别人做得更细。比如，想让一个动作看起来更和谐或更协调，我们会反复地调试和修改。
问：游戏行业有句话叫“快就是慢，慢就是快”。市场迭代很快，但一款好产品需要多年打磨。库洛怎么处理快与慢这对关系？
答： 快和慢代表了游戏行业的底层逻辑。我们选择了后者，快的本质是同质化竞争，我们做得慢是因为在做差异化定位。我们做产品可能做得慢，但在公司的整体发展、产品的迭代上，其实是快的。
问：游戏技术的迭代突破，对当下数字经济发展能起到哪些作用？
答： 我们对硬件的需求——比如对GPU以及GPU里芯片的需求，会推动相关行业发展。市场有需求，这个行业才会有真正发展的动力。
另外，游戏的发展对我们现在的AI有非常重要的促进作用。大世界AI或者叫物理AI，需要整个数字的仿真环境，数字仿真环境本质上是游戏里面的一个真实世界。在数字仿真世界里面进行数据采集和训练，它的成本会低很多。
问：从一个只有几人的小团队成长到如今的行业生力军，库洛游戏有哪些值得总结的企业文化？有怎样的企业愿景？
答： 库洛倡导“挑战即伟大”的企业文化。我们只有不断地自我挑战，才有可能在这个行业找到自己的位置。我们的愿景和使命从未改变：做这个星球上最好的游戏。
问：当东方美学融入数字幻境，国产游戏正在打通文化和科技融合的大门。库洛游戏的核心定位究竟是什么，它是一家游戏公司还是一家科技公司，亦或是一家文化公司？
答： 最核心的定位是游戏公司，但我们左手会跟科技握手、右手会跟文化握手。
问：数字游戏，为中华优秀传统文化打开了全新的表达窗口。在您看来，游戏的文化传播价值体现在哪里？
答： 《鸣潮》最近用中国传统舞蹈演绎了游戏内的一段音乐，整体的反馈效果非常好。玩家如果喜欢一个游戏，他自然就会喜欢这个游戏里面的文化表达。
另外，科幻是当代年轻人容易接受的一个叙事平台。它足够大，可以承载东方审美。我们自己在传统文化这个环境中成长起来，这也是我们擅长的一种表达方式。这两者的融合更像是在一个现代外表下对传统价值观的一个展示。我们希望全球玩家能够看到中国除了传统的、历史悠久的一面，也有很时尚、很酷、很有创造力的一面。
问：2025年，广东游戏产业营收超过2836亿元，占据全国八成市场份额。在您看来，大湾区为游戏产业的发展提供了哪些发展条件？
答： 一个公司再强也很难把所有事情都做下来，它需要产业链配套，我们的产业链上下游是非常好的。在研发和发行的各个环节，可以大量地和本地的公司合作。
广东乃至大湾区是做游戏非常好的地方，在全国都是领先的。很多优秀人才集聚在这里，这个地方很适合大家长线发展。未来好的游戏，大概率会出自广东。
问：您怎样看待游戏产业的发展前景？
答： 游戏产业是未来重要的产业之一，它是参与精神世界的一个重要行业。我觉得将来会迎来更大的市场，也期待未来有更多有梦想、有创造力的游戏公司涌现出来。
从制造业高地到产业福地，大湾区的深厚积淀正托起国产游戏的腾飞，推动游戏赋能千行百业。中国游戏的时代长卷，才刚刚拉开序幕。

title: 腾网米押注大模型1000亿融资创纪录；26Q4超20款大厂新作正面刚｜HOT周报
text:
能力、生态都很重要
一、核心观点
不知不觉间，国庆假期已经进入尾声。据交通运输部预计，国庆7天假期全社会跨区域人员流动量将达21.3亿人次，平均每天约3亿人次，约为平时的1.7倍。假期首日高速公路车流量有望达到7100万辆次，创历年国庆节单日流量新高。
在庞大的出行规模之外，年轻人的假期消费也在向展会、演出和IP体验等兴趣场景延伸。游戏行业自然没有错过这个节点。在今年的国庆黄金周期间，多款头部长线产品更新版本，上海、广州等地的游戏展会、音乐会等线下活动同样接连举行，线上流量与线下消费同步升温。
在假期结束后，市场也不会马上冷却。接下来的新游测试和上线档期已经一路排到了10月中旬，厂商在新品、研发团队与海外业务上的动作同样没有停下，例如腾讯的两款产品《怪物猎人：旅人》与《异人之下》，前者将在10月29日上线国际服，明年发布国服；后者将于11月4日进行“终局测试”。同时，还有更多品类的产品将要下场混战，那么，在这个刚刚结束的国庆假期里，哪些产品真正承接了假日流量？游戏厂商又在为接下来的Q4准备什么？
1.腾网米三七完美全力押注大模型竞争，创业公司单轮融资超1000亿
10月6日，彭博社援引知情人士消息称，DeepSeek即将完成至少800亿元的新一轮融资，最终规模可能接近1000亿元，腾讯与宁德时代是出资规模最大的投资方之一。路透社随后通过独立信源确认，DeepSeek获得的投资承诺已经超过800亿元，融资预计于10月完成。
腾讯此前已经参与DeepSeek首轮外部融资。与此同时，公司2026年第二季度资本开支达到528亿元，同比增长176%，主要投入AI算力、模型和云服务。腾讯一边建设混元、WorkBuddy和微信AI等自有体系，一边继续投资外部头部模型；值得一提的是，9月底，上半年爆火的龙虾类项目QClaw，宣布停止运营并可将数据迁移至WorkBuddy，也反映腾讯的AI业务正在由多线试验转向资源整合。
米哈游对AI的投入也格外重视，9月底，米哈游总裁大伟哥在交大的宣讲会上表示，米哈游投入1000亿在AI上，未来2到3年之内，米哈游都会是国产大模型团队里举足轻重的一员。米哈游近期也频繁释放着自己在AI方面的动作，给《崩坏：星穹铁道》里的列车长帕姆接入AI对话能力，《星布谷地》中的老板娘可以AI对话引起玩家热议，新作《Varsapura》则全方位探索AI Gameplay。米哈游内部也搭建了用来托管代码Agent和相关工具的生态平台EchoX，此外，还包括外部持续投资MiniMax等动作。
在AI布局这方面，腾讯与米哈游算是跑得特别快的，但其他游戏公司也正在形成自己的路线。例如网易同样参与了DeepSeek的首轮融资，并通过伏羲实验室搭建自己的游戏AI体系，官方数据显示，伏羲实验室已经发表200余篇AI顶会论文、提交600余项专利，相关能力服务200多家客户，日均调用超过1亿次。但同时，其对AI的侧重点也偏向于游戏内落地，例如《逆水寒》《永劫无间》《燕云十六声》等游戏内均有AI落地。
再比如三七互娱，其动作更多集中在投资等资本领域。据媒体统计，三七互娱近三年参投14只产业基金，其中12只投向游戏以外的赛道，仅2026年上半年便参与5只新基金，覆盖智谱、月之暗面、百川智能、量子计算、半导体、算力和光学硬件等方向。公司也已将GLM-4用于游戏剧情研发等。
完美世界则采取基金投资与业务协同并行的路线。今年8月至9月，公司先后以LP身份认购三只投向新兴科技领域的基金，合计出资超过6亿元；同时参与AI 3D大模型公司VAST的融资，向与游戏研发联系更紧密的3D生成、世界模型等方向布局。公司半年报显示，数字人视频、2D转3D等AI工具也已进入研发管线。
可以说，头部游戏公司都将AI大模型视作未来重要的竞争方向与能力项，在投资与自研方面也均有布局，在AI为游戏生产提效的同时，各家游戏公司也在加速探索AI Gameplay的新范式与新可能。
2.腾讯完美西山居等厂商节后出牌，Q4进入多品类混战
10月8日至17日，国内市场将迎来长假后的首轮产品集中节点。拾异游戏《七界梦谭》、凉屋游戏《查无此地》、上海竹子绿梦《绿梦：时空之声》、完美世界游戏《淡墨水云乡》和西山居《剑侠世界4：无限》将陆续测试或上线。腾讯《异人之下》也将在10月15日开启终极测试资格招募，正式测试定于11月4日。
10月15日是其中最密集的一天。《绿梦：时空之声》《剑侠世界4：无限》将全平台公测，《淡墨水云乡》开启小规模删档付费测试。在此之前，《七界梦谭》于10月9日开测，《查无此地》于10月14日登陆Steam抢先体验。
几款产品覆盖横版动作、二次元、武侠MMO、国风模拟经营、仙诡MMO和PVE搜打撤。它们虽然并非同品类直接对撞，但仍会同时争夺平台推荐、社区讨论和玩家时间。
此外，Q4后半程还有更受关注的产品入场。国产单机《影之刃零》定档10月29日，天美产品《怪物猎人：旅人》的国际服同样定档在这一天，国服预计于明年发布；《异人之下》随后开启测试并定档今年12月上线；《GTA6》则将在11月19日发售；竞争激烈的生活模拟品类中，米哈游《星布谷地》已定档12月上线，腾讯游戏《粒粒的小人国》正处于二测阶段，其他同类产品或也将加快产品进度；同时据市场预测，今年Q4可能还有1-2款大型二次元游戏上线，包括射击、微恐搜打撤等品类Q4大概率也会迎来更多的新品动作。不完全统计，今年Q4至少有超20款重磅新品将迎来新一轮测试或正式上线。
3.上海广州集结百余IP，黄金周线下竞争从展会延伸至城市文旅
10月2日至6日，小红书RED LAND 2026在上海复兴岛举行。本届活动面积超过10万平方米，集结《王者荣耀》《原神》《崩坏：星穹铁道》《黑神话：悟空》《鸣潮》等100多个游戏、动漫及娱乐IP，参与IP数量较上届翻倍，在RED LAND最后一天，米哈游总裁大伟哥和上海迪士尼总裁也到场参与了花车巡游环节。据相关报道，本次活动持票用户中约七至八成来自上海以外地区，游戏活动正在直接转化为跨城出行和假日消费。
同期，B站连续第三年举办了WF上海国际手办模型文化博览会，吸引超过400家品牌展商和2700名个人创作者参与，两日参与总人次预计突破15万。此外，深蓝互动也在上海体育馆举办《重返未来：1999》首次大型线下音乐会“众声漫游夜”，声量不俗。
在广州，AGF亚洲游戏博览会与CICF动漫游戏盛典也在假期内举行。《三角洲行动》《暗区突围》《逆战：未来》《湮灭之潮》《鸣潮》等产品集中参展，覆盖射击、二次元和国产单机等品类。
从平台组织的综合活动、单一产品的专场演出，到区域性游戏展会，游戏厂商的线下竞争正在形成不同层次。线下活动承担的功能也不再只是宣传新品，而是把IP体验、玩家社交、周边消费和城市旅游连接起来，争夺玩家整个假期的时间与消费预算。
4.拳头在广州成立全资子公司，SLG与UE5动作项目同步推进
公开信息显示，拳头游戏已在广州成立全资子公司傲拳（广州）网络科技有限公司，并开始招聘主策、原画、技术美术、QA及客户端开发等岗位。从招聘规模和岗位构成来看，拳头的广州团队或许正试着搭建更为完善的研发能力。
招聘信息显示，广州团队至少涉及两个尚未正式公布的项目。其中“代号Griffin”定位为城建SLG，招聘要求涉及城市成长、建筑升级和资源流转等系统；“Riot Discovery”则是一款使用虚幻引擎5开发、支持多人联机的第三人称动作游戏，由拳头北美、澳洲和中国团队共同参与研发，玩法侧重运镜、连招和Boss战等PVE内容。
拳头过去的核心优势主要集中在竞技和卡牌品类。广州团队同时探索城建SLG与多人动作游戏，说明公司正在尝试把IP、全球研发体系和服务型游戏经验带入更多赛道。对于腾讯而言，这也相当于补充了一支具备全球协作能力的研发团队。不过，新团队能否将拳头的IP积累和服务型游戏经验带入这些赛道，还要等待项目的更多信息。

六、一周大事件
海外行业动态 ：

前索尼互动娱乐总裁肖恩·莱登近日谈及索尼计划自2028年起停止为PlayStation新作发行实体光盘的决定。他认为，虽然数字版已经成为主流，但仍坚持购买实体游戏的用户往往是品牌最忠实的核心玩家，部分玩家还具有较强的收藏需求。全面转向数字发行不仅可能引发游戏所有权争议，也可能对PlayStation的品牌声誉造成影响。
下周（2026年10月7日-10月17日）开测新游：
下周（10月7日-10月17日）开测或上线的新游中，重点产品包括拾异游戏《七界梦谭》、凉屋游戏《查无此地》、上海竹子绿梦《绿梦：时空之声》、完美世界游戏《淡墨水云乡》、西山居《剑侠世界4：无限》、金山世游《猫咪和汤：魔法与美食》、梧桐宇舟《对峙：交锋时刻》。
由拾异游戏开发的《七界梦谭》前身名为《代号：界》，游戏最初由FunPlus孵化，由前网易《一梦江湖》主策甜少担任制作人，此后，紫龙也加入投资。近年来，MMO品类新品突围者仍在少数，并且题材仍大多局限于传统仙侠与日式奇幻等。《七界梦谭》在此上选用了近年来较为火热的“中式怪谈”，或许可以成功带来新的市场反馈。
凉屋游戏方面，《查无此地》将于10月14日登陆Steam抢先体验。游戏采用俯视角PVE搜打撤框架，玩家需要在超自然维度碎片中搜集物资并完成撤离。该作曾进入Steam新品节热门试玩榜前列，是本期值得关注的国产独立产品。
上海竹子绿梦研发的《绿梦：时空之声》将于10月15日在安卓、iOS和PC平台同步公测。产品巧妙地选择了一条横版动作+二次元+近未来废土与银河恶魔城相结合的道路，同样是近期值得关注的二次元品类产品之一。
西山居《剑侠世界4：无限》同样定档10月15日全平台公测。该作为剑侠世界系列新作，游戏将延续家族群战、自由交易和武侠MMO社交体系，并支持移动端与PC端数据互通。目前游戏在资深玩家群中关注较高，未来相信也会给IP注入新的活力。
完美世界游戏《淡墨水云乡》将于10月15日开启“归舟测试”。本次测试为PC与安卓平台的小规模删档付费测试，持续至10月30日，产品主打水墨美术、田园经营和自由建造。游戏的上一次露面还是在2024年时期，这一次或许会有新的变化。
《对峙：交锋时刻》将于10月16日开启国服限量首测，该作为海外移动FPS《对峙2》的国服版本，游戏目前已经在海外平稳运营过九年，去年末在欧洲地区的单周预估收入达到约56.86万美元（约合四百万人民币），季度活跃用户从580万增长至860万，可以说是国内手游FPS中不可忽视的“新挑战者”。

title: 今年哪款游戏，让你承认自己看走眼了？
text:
大多数时候，我们还是能猜个八九不离十的，但总会有一些意想不到的翻车时刻。而今年，这种看走眼的时候好像还挺多的……总有些产品上线前就被说暴死，但上线后的表现出乎意料地好。
从最早的 1 月说起，《明日方舟：终末地》就很典型——这游戏引导流程相对长，节奏相对慢，玩法对大众来说还相对陌生，所以开服流水即使低点，我觉得也情有可原。结果上线第一天，它就冲上了畅销榜 Top 5。
类似的产品，还包括 3 月上线的《洛克王国：世界》，这个游戏的付费做得非常克制，前期你甚至找不到什么花钱的理由……但仅仅到了第二天，游戏就直接登顶了畅销榜，让我们大部分人都没反应过来。
展开剩余
62%
更多的产品，实际上没这么大开大合的节奏，比如 4 月上线的《异环》，开服时并没有做到一波冲上 Top 10，但之后在大版本的更新中，却一度来到 Top 5 的位置，这也是很不容易的事。
一直到最近，《王者万象棋》的成绩也让很多人没想到——毕竟这种纯玩法向游戏，适应玩法本身就有门槛，而且理论上零氪也能玩。但畅销榜 Top 5 的成绩，还是有点让人意想不到的。
不过在另一面……也有些上线前被寄予厚望，公测表现却不尽如人意的产品。 其中不乏一些研发多年、成本巨大，但开局并不理想的大作。
当然了，游戏行业在某些时候……并不是只看开局就盖棺定论的。想想以前，很多大作也是开局不利，但后来靠持续运营、调优，以及新内容逆袭的。像《蛋仔派对》《超自然行动组》，都是这样的例子。
另一方面来说，一款游戏上线时的成绩，也受到诸多因素影响。比如宣发、舆情、前期引导，甚至是那几天有没有其他大作更新大版本……这也决定了，即使你经验再丰富，也很难打包票说没有一款产品看走眼。
所以在今年，哪款游戏让你承认自己看走眼了？

title: Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery operating under Skydance following completion of $111bn merger
text:
Paramount has completed its $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, with both companies now operating under the name Skydance.
Skydance's announcement does not reference video games. However, co-CEO Ynon Kreiz addressed the segment's role in a separate statement to The Hollywood Reporter .
"We will have plenty of opportunities to develop new businesses, products, games and experiences to engage fans wherever they are and be where the consumer is going," said Kreiz.
Addressing staff, Skydance CEO David Ellison stated that the merger would require making "difficult decisions."
"Bringing together two companies of this size and complexity will require difficult decisions. There will be changes, and there will be impacts. I'm not going to pretend otherwise," said Ellison.
"What I can promise you is that we will move through those decisions as quickly and thoughtfully as we can. We will communicate directly. We will tell you what we know when we know it. And we will not allow a prolonged integration process to distract us from the reason we brought these companies together in the first place: which is to build the next-generation media and entertainment company."
Skydance is targeting more than $6 billion in "synergy savings", which it said will "come primarily from technology, integration and procurement, marketing and real estate rationalisation."
Earlier this summer, Skydance launched Paramount Game Studio by merging Skydance Interactive and Skydance New Media.
GamesIndustry.biz caught up with EVP Dan Prigg about the studio's goals and upcoming projects from Platinum and Amy Hennig, such as 1943: Rise of Hydra and a new Star Wars title with Lucasfilm.
With the merger complete, Skydance now owns Warner's intellectual property, including Avalanche Software (Hogwarts Legacy) and its publishing label Portkey Games, NetherRealm (Mortal Kombat), Rocksteady (Arkham), and TT Games (Lego). The acquisition also includes studios such as WB Games Montreal, WB Games New York, and WB Games San Francisco.
You can read our full timeline of the Warner Bros acquisition process here .

title: GamesIndustry.biz to host panel at Game Republic's Investment Summit at MCM Comic Con October 2026
text:
GamesIndustry.biz will host a panel during Game Republic's Investment Summit at MCM Comic Con later this month.

title: Asha Sharma reportedly informs staff that Xbox has "started to return to growth" during internal town hall
text:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reportedly held an internal town hall, telling staff that "after an all time low, we've started to return to growth."
According to Windows Central , Sharma said Xbox is "making the right decisions to reinvest in the business."
"After an all-time low, we've started to return to growth, more than two to three times what we were, and we expect that to continue."
While Sharma did not specify exact figures, she noted that Xbox has returned to growth in its first-party segment and stabilised user engagement after earlier declines this year.
Recent releases such as Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2, and World of Warcraft Forever reportedly had strong launches. Sharma also reiterated her goal to " evolve Game Pass into a more flexible system ," following significant declines in the service under previous leadership.
Elsewhere, Sharma said its next-gen hardware Project Helix will be a family of devices rather than a single console, as "there is not one device that fits all."
"We will certainly have a great console first, but we also know that many players will be on the go. There are some things that we are the best in the world to manufacture, and there are other things that we will partner on. So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this."
As for this generation, Sharma stated Xbox needs to invest more in console despite the segment's current stagnant growth. She said the key to strengthening Xbox Series X|S is to continue investing in cloud gaming , its disc-to-digital program , and its Play Anywhere initiative.
Last week, Sharma reiterated that "Xbox is not for sale" after speculation that the company could be spun out as a separate business rather than remaining under Microsoft.
"We will do whatever it takes to set the company up for success, and we will look at the right partnerships, the right operating model and everything needed to achieve that," said Sharma.
This comes as Xbox continues its restructuring initiative, which has resulted in a 20% reduction in the Xbox workforce and the closure or divestiture of several studios .
Xbox also reorganized a handful of its studios , transferring Rare and the Halo franchise to Activision, integrating Obsidian into Bethesda, and merging Turn 10 with Playground Games.

title: Unity unveils a web-based AI game creation platform
text:
Today marks the launch of Playground, a new Google platform for generating games using natural language prompts, and it will soon host a version of Unity based around generative AI agents.
Unity Spark , which runs on the Unity engine, will be launching in beta later this year. The tool will allow users to design and iterate on 3D games via text prompts, and it is entirely browser-based, with no download required. Both Unity Spark and Playground will only be available to users aged 18+.
Although announced as a strategic partnership with Google, Unity Spark will use a variety of generative AI models, and is not exclusively tied to Google's AI technology.
Unity Spark is linked to the Unity Asset Store; in a demo given to GamesIndustry.biz , a text prompt asking for a cape for the main character brought up a range of suggested items from the store. Another prompt asked for a sunrise background, and the AI agent provided a range of options. The agent can also make suggestions based on the user's actions, such as offering to create a tool for toggling between different lighting presets, and multiple agents can be set to work at the same time.
Watch on YouTube
In a blog post , Unity CEO Matt Bromberg said that Unity Spark wasn't about "one-shotting" – that is, generating an entire game from a single prompt – and is instead about building something "worth working on, polishing, and sharing."
"It's about using the new technology to enable more people to express themselves," he said. "And it all begins with the game art. Unity Spark connects directly to the Unity Asset Store, so you can build with thousands of high-quality, artist-created assets made by our community.
"We made Unity Spark for the gamers who have spent a thousand hours inside a genre and know exactly what's missing. The graphic artist who wants to bring their vision to life but doesn't know how to code. Modders who now want to create something entirely new. That's the opportunity we see: Folks with real creative conviction who can now fulfill their full potential."
Multiple users can work on the same project at the same time by sharing a link, and projects can be published on Google Playground. The Unity Spark editor only runs on desktop browsers, but games made with the system can be played on both desktop and mobile browsers.
At launch, it won't be possible to download projects or export them to the full desktop version of the Unity engine. It also won't be possible to sell any projects created with Unity Spark at launch.
Payment for Unity Spark will involve a credit-based system, which is tied to AI tokens. Access to a certain amount of credits will be free, after which users will have to buy credits, although the full details of the payment system haven't been finalised. But rather than being designed to generate a profit, Unity's main aim for the system is to encourage more people to make games.
"Electronic games are the last major form of entertainment that nearly everyone consumes but almost nobody creates"
"Producing a polished experience of your own has long been beyond the capabilities of most people," said Bromberg.
"As a consequence, although about 3 billion people play a game made with Unity each month, almost none of them have ever made one. Electronic games are the last major form of entertainment that nearly everyone consumes but almost nobody creates. That's something we'd like to help change.
"We don't know exactly who will walk through this door, or what they'll make. That's the whole point. Democratizing game creation is Unity's founding mission. Unity Spark was incubated in that spirit. We can't wait to see what you build together."
Unity has been steadily building a suite of generative AI tools for its game engine. A number of them were launched in open beta in May , including a 'Plan' mode for designing implementation steps and 'Skills' for guidance in areas like UI creation.
In August, Bromberg credited the company's growth in revenue to the ongoing success of Unity Vector AI . The upcoming Unity 7, which launches in Q1 2027, will feature AI tools as a core component, although Unity's senior vice president of product Adam Smith has emphasised that developers are not required to use them . "If your studio has committed to keeping AI out of your creative work – you're not on the sidelines of this release," he said.

title: How to run an indie game studio: Part 2, Defining your future
text:
Last week, we established what a studio is, and how understanding its core components can help you find your studio's purpose . This week, we're going to start on the FIRM framework proper, starting with the first pillar, which concerns your studio's future. Because the next most important question after "why do we exist?" is "where are we going?"
Deciding as a team where you want the studio to go in the future is one of the most important acts of alignment in any studio. Whatever long-term goal you define will set the boundaries for every other decision you make from that point on. We'll look at this first, before discussing how to use that long-term goal to set better yearly goals.
The long-term goal: Your BHAG
A helpful tool for thinking about your studio's future comes from Jim Collins – the same Jim Collins we borrowed the Hedgehog Concept from last week . In his 1994 book Built to Last , Collins coined the term Big Hairy Audacious Goal, or BHAG (pronounced "Bee-HAG") for short. Through his research, Collins found that this singular, clear, and ambitious goal for a company's future is one of the things that separates sustainably successful companies from those that flounder.
Whenever you make a big decision, your BHAG gives you a frame to evaluate it against
A well-defined long-term goal like the BHAG complements and supports your studio purpose, and fulfils a similar role: it helps you make better decisions, attract the right people, and be more intentional about what you do and how you do it. Whenever you make a big decision for the studio – for example, deciding what your next game should be, whether to self-publish, or what the right team size is for the studio – your BHAG gives you a frame to evaluate it against. You simply ask, "Does this get us closer to where we want to go, or not?"
Finding your BHAG is relatively simple, thanks to an exercise devised by Collins himself. Start by agreeing on a date in the future: the 10–25 years suggested by Collins is an eternity in our industry, and through my work I've found that 5–10 years works well for most studios. Then, each person on the team writes a brief article that will be published on that future date. Be specific in the details: where is the article published? Is it on Game Developer, GamesIndustry.biz, Forbes, or Quote? Think about the main reason the article is being written: what milestone warranted this specific article? Include as many details as you can about what the studio has achieved by then, and why they matter to the overall trajectory of the studio.
Then, gather as a team and read these articles to each other, discussing which elements resonated, where you might already be in agreement, and where your opinions differ. Finally, discuss which of the shared achievements would make for the best overarching goal. You're looking for something ambitious enough to stretch you, specific enough to mean something, and resonant enough that everyone in the room feels it.
Your BHAG should be like the mountain in Journey; a clear, shared goal that will take significant effort to reach | Image credit: Thatgamecompany
There are no right or wrong answers here. For some studios, their BHAG might be expressed in downloads or units sold, for others it's being recognized with an international award, and for others still it's measured in their impact across the industry. Whatever your goal turns out to be, make sure it's clear and compelling, measurable and, crucially, between 50% and 70% doable. This ensures that you have to put genuine effort into reaching the goal, stretching you beyond your current capabilities.
The yearly goals: Making progress real
If the BHAG is the summit of the mountain you're trying to climb, yearly goals are like the camps you pitch on the way. Yearly goals help you transform the ambition of your BHAG into traction by defining the major steps needed to get there. They keep your team focused on the things that truly matter and help you stay accountable, and the mere act of figuring out the goals that matter helps to foster alignment.
Setting five to seven goals forces you to prioritise the things that actually matter
For most studios, I've found that the sweet spot is somewhere between five and seven goals for the year. Fewer than that and you risk setting the bar too low from the outset; more than that and you risk spreading your efforts too thin to actually finish the things you started. Five to seven forces you to prioritise the things that actually matter, and that you can actually finish. As a rule, you're not done until you've cut something that, after discussion, turns out to be a nice-to-have rather than a must-have.
When everyone agrees that you've identified the right goals for making progress towards your BHAG, and that hitting these goals would constitute a successful year, you know you've got the right list.
Intentional work follows intentional goals
Your purpose is the reason your studio exists. Your BHAG tells everyone where the studio is going. And your yearly goals state what you're finishing this year to get there. Together, these three things form the spine of intentional studio leadership, and help you transform from reacting to outside forces to proactively shaping your own future.
This week's homework
Together with your team, work through the following:
Find your BHAG. Agree on a date in the future, and each write a brief article detailing the things you'd want to have achieved by then. Share your articles, find the common threads, and work together to define one overarching long-term goal that everyone can rally behind.
Set your yearly goals. With your BHAG in mind, define between five and seven goals for the coming year. For each one, ask yourself: does achieving this bring us meaningfully closer to our long-term goal? If the answer is no, reconsider whether it belongs on the list.
Next week, we'll get into the second pillar of the FIRM framework, and look at how to surface and solve the issues that inevitably get in the way of your studio's progress.
Want the full FIRM framework with step-by-step implementation instructions? Visit martijnvanzwieten.com/firm to download the free template.
Martijn van Zwieten is a business and leadership coach, and the creator of the FIRM and LoGOS studio management methods. He has coached over 150 CEOs, founders, and leaders to build better studios, ranging from indie darlings like Rusty Lake and Twirlbound to AAA powerhouses like Bethesda Game Studios and MachineGames.

title: Paramount Games Studio and WB Games merge under Skydance following completion of $111bn acquisition
text:
Paramount Games Studio and Warner Bros. Games will merge into one unit under Skydance overseen by Tony Driscoll.
Earlier today, Paramount completed its $111 billion acquisition of WBD , resulting in both companies operating under the name Skydance.
The initial announcement did not refer to its video game divisions. However, in a memo obtained by Variety , Skydance president Andy Gordon announced that Paramount and WBD's games and experiences divisions will merge to oversee projects based on both companies' IP.
Driscoll, president of Paramount Games Studio, will also lead games and experiences, in addition to heading corporate strategy and development at Skydance.
"We're investing in our future growth engines alongside our core ambitions in TV, Film and direct-to-consumer: Games, Experiences, Consumer Products, and Publishing," said Gordon.
"These are core pillars of our strategy to build engagement and fandom in both the physical and digital worlds. We want to meet consumers where they watch, play, and engage. At the same time, we see opportunities to build on DC Comics' storytelling and expand our e-commerce offerings to connect fans with the brands they love."
Paramount Games Studio was established this summer and is led by EVP and head of games Dan Prigg. The studio combines Paramount's IP with Skydance Interactive and Skydance New Media.
"Paramount, prior to the merger, was just licensing," Prigg told GamesIndustry.biz . "They weren't doing any internal development. They weren't really doing much in terms of co-development and publishing. Skydance had a couple of studios, and we had licensing on our own."
It was concluded that "one division can help control the slate, help with the brands, [and] really build the communities."
As part of the merger, Josh Silverman has been appointed president of global products and publishing. Jim Sterner will remain chief people officer, and Jose Turkienicz will continue as president of global operations.
In the initial announcement, Skydance CEO David Ellison stated that the merger will require the company to make "difficult decisions," including "changes and impacts."
"Bringing together two companies of this size and complexity will require difficult decisions. There will be changes, and there will be impacts. I'm not going to pretend otherwise," said Ellison.
"What I can promise you is that we will move through those decisions as quickly and thoughtfully as we can. We will communicate directly. We will tell you what we know when we know it. And we will not allow a prolonged integration process to distract us from the reason we brought these companies together in the first place: which is to build the next-generation media and entertainment company."

title: Wizards of the Coast union expands, demands company stop pushing generative AI
text:
The Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering teams at Wizards of the Coast are unionizing, and are calling on Hasbro and Wizards leadership to stop pushing generative AI.
According to IGN , the Wizards of the Coast-CWA (UWOTC-CWA) is expanding to include the D&D team and Team X, which works on Magic: The Gathering and Duel Masters.
Wizards has until October 13 to voluntarily recognize the expanded unit.
The company did not voluntarily recognize the union when it covered only the Arena team, which unionized in April and has since won its union election . If Hasbro declines again, the union would have to file with the National Labor Relations Board and win another election.
In a petition setting out its demands, the union writes: "Leadership, without regard for the desires of our teams, has pushed for adoption of LLMs and generative AI. This has to stop; our teams deserve a robust and enforceable AI policy that aligns with our goals and values."
The union is also demanding ownership of what employees create outside of work, as it did in its April announcement letter.
"Currently, if an employee makes anything creative in their free time, with their own resources, Hasbro may claim ownership," the letter said. "What we do in our free time should not be dictated by the company; neither should what we make in our free time be owned by the company."
In May, Wizards of the Coast and Hasbro missed the deadline to voluntarily recognize a union formed by Magic: The Gathering Arena developers . Later that same month, WotC wrote to its employees to warn that unionizing could mean staff "end up with more, the same or less than [they] have now," and suggested that "your voice is strongest when it is heard directly."

title: Undead Labs studio head says they were 'irresponsibly transparent' in preparing staff for layoffs
text:
Studio head Philip Holt says he was being incredibly candid with employees as layoffs loomed.
Undead Labs, the studio behind the State of Decay titles and the in-development S tate of Decay 3 , has had a rocky few months since Xbox announced plans to divest the studio from its Xbox Game Studios portfolio back in July. In the intervening months, the studio has faced the specter of layoffs as it transitions from an Xbox studio to an independent one, and studio leadership has weathered this turbulence by being candid with the team.
In an interview with The Game Business , Undead Labs studio head Philip Holt explained that he has tried to be open and clear with the studio that layoffs were likely coming as part of the Xbox divestiture and pivot to independent ownership— which they did in late September .
“Rather than keeping them in the dark and manufacture some alternate reality, I just brought them alongside," Holt told The Game Business. "That probably reduced some anxiety. I tried to put myself in their shoes. You’re not in control, you don’t really know what’s happening, you know your job might be at risk, and you’re wondering if this game is actually going to finish. So, I tried to share as much as I could. We had pretty direct conversations. We talked early on that under probably any scenario, there’d be job losses. On the day of the layoff, people were prepared. That ended up being a real courtesy, as painful as it was. Nobody wants to lose a job, but I think people understood the reason."
Related: Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor brings back 'over half' of furloughed staff
Providing advanced notice for mass layoffs is the backbone of the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) act in California, requiring a 60-day notice period for companies with over 75 employees barring penalties for employers that violate it. Though Undead Labs is located in Washington, the same value principles on layoffs seem to apply here. The reasoning at the time of passing was that it provides a chance for employees to search for other employment before being left out in the cold.
Holt would not confirm the specific number of job losses, arguing that turns the layoffs into a statistic and takes the view away from the people who were let go, but the studio confirmed on LinkedIn that the layoffs were "significant." After separating from Microsoft, Undead Labs took itself independent, and retained the State of Decay property.
Undead Labs is currently working on State of Decay 3 , a zombie survival game announced under the Xbox banner in 2020, two years after Microsoft acquired the studio. Despite the layoffs, Holt insists that the game is still on target for a 2027 release.
Related: Former Activision Blizzard CEO Bobby Kotick named to the board of post-merger Skydance
Update 10/7: This story has been updated with the correct spelling of Undead Labs' studio name.

title: GameStop, other retailers to sell used PlayStation 5 Pro units for 66 percent over MSRP
text:
The advanced PlayStation 5 console is already both highly sought-after and hard to find. Now retailers are pricing it well above MSRP.
Developers targeting the higher-end PlayStation 5, which boasts graphical features that run games smoother at higher resolutions, may soon be limited to audiences of only high-income enthusiasts. Retailers and third-party sellers have suddenly jumped in price on the PlayStation 5 Pro, indicating demand for the console exceeds the current supply.
Last night, users on the GameStop subreddit began sharing what appeared to be an internal company email advising employees of a price change on PlayStation 5 Pro units brought in for trade-in and sold back as used. GameStop would sell back the PlayStation 5 Pro units for $1,399.99 for digital versions or $1,499.99 for versions with the disc add-on attached. Color variations, like the Wolverine Yellow SKUs, would be priced in line with those numbers.
These rumors were confirmed today on GameStop's store page when used prices for the PlayStation 5 Pro were updated. Similarly, third-party sellers on Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart have all raised their prices to match this increase.
Related: Naughty Dog is working on new The Last Of Us 'projects'
This represents a 60 - 66 percent increase over the manufacturer's suggested retail price, though it should be noted that PlayStation 5 Pro units from PlayStation's direct-sale store are currently unavailable, as are the disc add-on attachments. It is also a 100% increase over the PlayStation 5 Pro's launch price of $699.99, a price point that has steadily ticked up since 2024 as RAM and storage prices increase due to an ongoing AI crunch.
Sony's competitors, Nintendo and Microsoft, are faring little better in the face of hardware shortages, with Xbox increasing prices multiple times over the last two years . Nintendo, meanwhile, just enacted the Switch 2's first price increase in the United States, with the company's president warning that a long-term memory shortage may "put pressure on profitability."
The reason that PlayStation 5 Pros specifically are spiking in price likely has a lot to do with Grand Theft Auto 6 . The upcoming Rockstar title is promising to be one of the biggest video game launches of all time and does support the PlayStation 5 Pro's higher graphical ceiling, with the PlayStation 5 store page advertising that the game is "PS5 Pro Enhanced."
Those who have yet to jump into the current console generation but plan for the latest Grand Theft Auto may find themselves priced out of a market that's getting more expensive, not less.

title: Google debuts new 'experimental' AI game platform named Google Playground
text:
A platform for people who want to play games made by AI.
Google is making another big swing at building a dedicated video game platform—this time opting to produce one for games made with generative AI. The new venture, Google Playground, is a platform for making, sharing, and playing games made using generative AI tools.
In today's announcement, a Google spokesperson described Playground as an "experimental gaming platform" that "Lets users create, play and share fully custom games with no coding experience required.
"With Playground’s conversational interface, users can create custom games by typing what they want, remixing starter prompts or getting guided support to help them share their creativity with the world," the company stated. "Essentially acting as a director, users can refine the rules with prompts, customize characters and tweak the environment until it’s what they envision. And since Playground is browser-based, games are playable across phones and laptops."
Related: Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor brings back 'over half' of furloughed staff
Developers interested in experimenting with Playground can also take advantage of Unity Spark , a new, separately-announced tool from Unity built to work with Playground.
Google's new platform appears targeted to both veteran game developers and would-be game-makers who want to turn their ideas into games without going through the traditional development process. This comes as developers continue to experiment with generative AI , but do so with grave concerns about its impact on the video game industry.
Those curious about Google's new platform can try the games for themselves here .

title: Unity unveils Unity Spark, an prompt-based tool for Google's AI game platform
text:
Unity's new tool allows prompt-based game development, working in collaboration with Google AI.
Unity, one of game development's preeminent engine creators, has announced a strategic partnership with Google to leverage AI for prompt-based game development for Google's AI platform, which is dubbed "Playground." As part of Playground's developer environment, Unity is introducing a new tool named Unity Spark , a user interface specifically built for making games with user-created prompts.
In a press release, Unity describes Spark as an "expanded creation experience," that is capable of "unlocking robust, professional-level mechanics, high-fidelity 3D capabilities, and the ultimate flexibility of Unity runtime." Unity goes on to describe Spark as beginning game development with a text prompt to "eventually" grow into full game experiences, skipping the step of coding.
"This isn't about 'one-shotting,' said Unity CEO Matthew Bromberg in a blog post accompanying the announcement. "Asking AI to regurgitate an already invented game does not make you the next Hideo Kojima, any more than re-typing the first paragraph of War and Peace in your word processor makes you Tolstoy."
Related: We're finally talking about AI, ft. David 'Rez' Graham and Luke Dicken
Spark, as part of a collaboration with Google, is exclusively for use with Google's AI platform, with the pair dubbing the entire environment Playground. Within the realm of Playground, developers using the tools can use Google's own publishing tools and share their work with others, as well as incorporate Google's own existing technologies for leaderboards, matchmaking, and community features.
"Unity Spark is about being able to create real, unique interactive experiences, Bromberg continued. "To build something worth working on, polishing, and sharing. It’s about using the new technology to enable more people to express themselves. And it all begins with the game art. Unity Spark connects directly to the Unity Asset Store, so you can build with thousands of high-quality, artist-created assets made by our community."
"We made Unity Spark for the gamers who have spent a thousand hours inside a genre and know exactly what’s missing. The graphic artist who wants to bring their vision to life but doesn’t know how to code. Modders who now want to create something entirely new. That's the opportunity we see: Folks with real creative conviction who can now fulfill their full potential."
Generative AI Still Controversial In Game Development
While the tool is a logical step for Unity, which has been AI-forward in its success , developer criticism of AI and its place within creation has been more mixed overall. Recent surveys indicate that creatives within the game industry are worried and cynical about generative AI for game development and its effect on the quality of games.
Related: Godot adoption is rising: what are devs getting out of the engine?
Unity itself has expressed a need for stronger guard rails on generative AI within its own tools after an employee used Unity Muse to generate an image of Disney's Mickey Mouse on an official live stream, prompting copyright concerns.
Moreover, from an audience perspective, developers are still assessing audience response to the use of generative AI tools in game development. Pocketpair, developers of the wildly successful Palworld , "doesn't believe in it" arguing that the audience will likely stay away from games that incorporate it . Valve's Steam, the largest PC gaming marketplace, requires a disclosure for AI tools or content used within a game that is then presented on each game's store page.
Earlier this year, Totally Human Media CEO Ichiro Lambe noted that over 8000 games on Steam featured the AI disclosure, but that disclosure does not seem to meaningfully affect the user review scores of games that bear one.
Developers can experiment with Playground for themselves today , and learn more about Unity Spark here .

title: Electronic Arts' leveraged buyout faces a bondholder battle
text:
The acquisition of Electronic Arts required taking on a lot of debt, and some bondholders are reportedly demanding more cash.
Electronic Arts, which recently transitioned from a public shareholder business to one owned by multiple private equity entities , still has creditors to answer to regarding previously-issued bonds, and a showdown with bondholders may be brewing for the publisher.
In August, Electronic Arts finalized a ( much-criticized ) acquisition by collaborating partners from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners, which is led by U.S. president Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner. To finance the buyout, the consortium borrowed $20 billion from JPMorgan, using that money as leveraged debt on the company.
The expectation then is that Electronic Arts would pay back that debt in the course of regular operations over the years. This is called a leveraged buyout and Electronic Arts holds the distinction of being the largest one of all time .
As The Wall Street Journal reports , however, this has its own complications. In taking on that level of debt from JPMorgan, the leverage increase potentially weakens EA's credit profile, leading to a loss in its investment grade rating. In such a scenario, legacy creditors now in the role of bondholders facing potential declines in bond value can demand that simply paying them back is not good enough and ask for a 101 percent repayment.
Related: Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor brings back 'over half' of furloughed staff
One group of bondholders is doing so for two $750 million tranches, totaling $1.5 billion.
To combat all of this, the Journal reports that EA is transforming its bonds into assets that resemble U.S. Treasury securities, essentially splitting the principal and the interest. This apparently has relatively little effect on the leveraged buyout. But it may not stem the tide in the bondholder revolt.
This continues an ongoing disapproval by bondholders for the acquisition after EA failed to buy back all their bonds in time earlier this year, as reported by Bloomberg .
For more details on the dispute, be sure to read The Wall Street Journal's full coverage .

Monopoly Go was the biggest advertiser among US mobile games in August, according to Sensor Tower estimates. Its $93.8m in US IAP revenue was also the highest of the 10.
Royal Match ranked seventh on ad spend but second on revenue with $64.8m, and was the only game in the top 10 with double digit download growth, up 13% month on month. Candy Crush Saga, a match 3 game, completed the top three for revenue with $53.0m.
Gossip Harbor and Kingshot ranked second and third on ad spend, but both lost more than 20% of their US downloads. Revenue was steadier, with four of the 10 growing, led by Tasty Travels at 7.2%. Pokémon Go saw the steepest drop, down 48% to $30.9m from a much stronger July.
Vita Mahjong was the outlier: tenth on ad spend and last on IAP revenue with $121k, but top for downloads with 1.40m. AppLovin was the top US network by impression share for Gossip Harbor, Royal Kingdom and Royal Match.
Turkish mobile devs earned $2.76bn in 2025 – up 450% since 2020
Mobile games made by Turkish developers brought in $2.76bn worldwide in 2025, up from $504m in 2020, according to a new report from Adjust .
That lifts Turkish studios’ share of the global mobile games market from 1% to 5%, while domestic player spending reached $347m.
Dream Games generated $1.7bn in 2025, and Royal Match and Royal Kingdom have earned more than $5.2bn combined since launch, says Adjust.
In the first half of 2026, mobile game sessions in Türkiye grew 6% year on year, with day 1 retention at 20%, day 7 at 6% and day 30 at 1%. Midcore games made up just 12% of installs but 51% of sessions, while hypercasual accounted for 53% of installs and 18% of sessions.
August’s top performers, according to Appfigures
Honor of Kings has been top of Appfigures’ top grossing charts for a while now. The data firm estimates that Tencent’s MOBA earned $108m after store fees in August.
Gossip Harbor took second place with $105m, the most the game has earned in a single month. Whiteout Survival ($104m), Royal Match ($95m) and PUBG Mobile ($88m) completed the top five, while Candy Crush Saga ($85m) and Monopoly Go ($78m) followed. The top 10 combined earned an estimated $861m.
On downloads, Roblox held the top spot in the combined iOS and Android charts with an estimated 20m installs, ahead of Subway Surfers on 18m.
Grand Games’ Block Out (9m installs) led the iOS top download charts in August, with Smash Fest (6m) second and Bus Traffic Fever third (6m). On Android, Roblox (15m), Subway Surfers (14m) and Block Blast (11m) led the way.
Food Hunt: Pixel Puzzle hits $9.7m
Funfinity’s hybridcasual sort puzzle game Food Hunt: Pixel Puzzle has earned an estimated $9.7m in lifetime revenue, according to AppMagic.
It made $1m in IAP revenue last week, compared to $1.9m for rival Colony Flow , which added its own ants-themed twist to the Pixel Flow mechanic.
Food Hunt overtook Colony Flow on weekly installs, with 1.67m against 1.4m. It launched almost a month earlier and introduced the ant concept first, but grew more slowly.
AppMagic suggests marketing may have played a role: Colony Flow’s top ad creatives generated more than 4x the impressions of Food Hunt.
Skillz’ owner Firy sells $55m stake in Photon maker Exit Games
Firy, the group that also owns Skillz, says it has sold its $55m stake in Photon maker Exit Games. Photon is the multiplayer tech behind games like Stumble Guys and Steam hit Peak.
Exit Games bought back the 10.5% stake from Firy on October 2, having taken investment from the Las Vegas-based group back in 2021.
Joygrid invests in Oddmar maker Mobge
Turkish early-stage VC firm Joygrid has announced an undisclosed investment in Oddmar maker Mobge, which apparently values the studio at $10m. The actual fee was not disclosed.
Mobge’s platformer Oddmar won an Apple Design Award in 2018.

title: Google reveals Playground, its AI-powered game-making platform
text:
Playground is Google’s new browser-based game creation platform. It invites players to create and edit games with a series of prompts, then share them with friends.
The AI-powered tool is live today for players aged 18 and over in the US. Google did not provide detail on launches outside the US, but did state that access will roll out soon for those signed up to Google One, its web service and AI subscription package.
Playground users will be able to start a new game project from scratch or remix starter prompts. The browser-based games can then be shared among friends or be published to the Playground Explore community gallery so others can play on mobile or PC. Leaderboards and multiplayer is also supported for certain genres, and existing Google Play Games users can log into the service with their existing profile.
Players can rate other users’ Playground games, and Google’s algorithms will surface games it feels are “fresh, creative, and fun”. All games go through a safety screening process and can be reported if they are considered to be breaking Google’s community rules.
Google Playground will also be integrated with Unity Spark for pro-level functionality. Google said the collab enables advanced mechanics, 3D capabilities and “the flexibility of the Unity runtime.”
Unity Spark was announced today at the same time as Google Playground, and offers a similar feature set. It is currently in testing, with a closed beta coming soon. A full launch for Unity Spark is coming later this year.
Playground is described by Google as “an experimental gaming platform” that follows on from the Project Genie demos it released back in January.
Project Genie allows users to create lightly interactive game worlds with just a prompt. Its unveiling sent shares of several major gaming stocks tumbling, including Roblox, Unity and Take-Two.
Facebook owner Meta recently announced a similar set of tools under its Horizon brand. Its Horizon Create app will allow players to create games with a prompt and publish them across Facebook and Instagram. It is currently in testing, and there’s no set launch date for the app just yet.
Google-owned YouTube has also been making moves in games recently; it expanded its YouTube Playables range of simple webgames to over 50 markets.

title: RED LAND是怎么把自己做成“二次元迪士尼”的？
text:
昨天，由小红书主办、为期5天的RED LAND正式结束。也是在这几天，一则关于RED LAND上NPC的帖子登上了小红书站内的热点话题：视频里，一位保洁阿姨在晚间清场时和一位NPC交谈了几句，NPC伸手用梳子为阿姨整理好了刘海，随后两个人开心地挥手告别，这段互动被路过的玩家拍了下来，成为了今年RED LAND最出圈的画面之一。
和保洁阿姨互动的NPC
这里的“NPC”指的是小红书打造的原创NPC“岛民”，在RED LAND的世界观里，这些NPC们是这座冒险岛世界观里的原住岛民，在整个RED LAND举办期间，你都会在现场的各处偶遇他们，完成互动任务，或者开展自由对话。这些NPC也是RED LAND从第一届开始就延续到现在的特色内容。
今年是RED LAND的第二届，场地依然在在上海杨浦滨江复兴岛，但展区面积从8万平方米扩展至15万平方米，参展IP数量超过160个。截至目前，官方尚未公布登岛人数统计，但从正式开展前的五轮开票全部售罄和社交媒体的反响来看，本届RED LAND的热度较去年应该有大幅度增高。
从办展资历来看，RED LAND无疑是一个新生展会。但作为上海近年涌现出的大型游戏主题线下活动，它在空间形态、展会定位上做出了和Bilibili World（BW）、ChinaJoy截然不同的尝试——整体以露天空间为主，将IP点位散布在岛屿的户外道路、旧厂房与岸线之间，展台活动外还有夜场演出、花车巡游等内容，这都让RED LAND很大程度剥离了商务属性和IP宣传属性，转而呈现给玩家一种“乐园”的感觉。
现场的花车游行环节
也因此，你会看到不少玩家在展会结束后评价RED LAND就像“一座二次元迪士尼”。与此同时，许多和NPC们有关的讨论也热度颇高，他们在一定程度上从后方加强了“乐园”的氛围，甚至无意中创造了很多偶然的动人瞬间。许多玩家都发现，这些NPC不止会承担指路、解答问题的基础工作，甚至还能够承接玩家的情绪倾诉。
前几天，触乐在RED LAND现场采访了本次RED LAND的NPC导演伞，并和RED LAND项目团队进行了交流。伞从首届RED LAND便参与了岛民的角色设定与NPC演绎导演的工作，而项目组团队则决定了RED LAND整个世界观的打造方向，以及今年NPC互动、花车模式创新和整体策展的内容。从和他们的对话中，我们或许可以知道：RED LAND是怎么把自己做成二次元届的“迪士尼”的？
■ 岛民
RED LAND“冒险岛”的世界观是完全的原创IP。世界观的整体是从第一届RED LAND就开始打造的，项目组成员告诉我，这个世界观也从最开始就支撑起了RED LAND所有创作的准则，“在一个存档了大家所有的次元美好记忆冒险岛上，主角需要通过积攒存档碎片，达成进度通关”，也因此，玩家们会在不同的展台获得存档碎片样式的“PIN”，会和冒险岛上的原住“岛民”（即NPC）互动。
今年，RED LAND岛民的数量有所增加，和去年相比，功能也从场地引导变得更倾向于互动，“基本每位NPC身上都有1个小副本，和自己的表演剧情”。这种变化的原因主要来自于第一届的用户反馈：在去年的RED LAND上，NPC更多是通过沉浸式的角色设定来指引玩家——当时的考量更多在于，整个户外场地确实非常大，玩家非常需要线下引导，而且这种NPC互动模式在国内也相当创新。
和玩家互动的岛民
在确定了世界观的前提下，项目组在具体创作内容上给了导演组非常大的自由度，“对故事、背景设定上都给了很多自由发挥的空间，核心目标是要让玩家足够开心”。伞说，这个过程有点像在做一个游戏副本，首先是确定游戏的世界观，然后结合地图（岛上的要素），设计NPC和为NPC编写人物小传。在他和整个导演团队的职业生涯中，这种依托于一个展会打造IP和世界观，都是从来没有过的经历。
第一届RED LAND的时候，项目组意外地发现，“岛民和主角之间发生了非常良好的互动，口碑也非常出圈”。这直接影响了他们在今年RED LAND的决策：在世界观不变的前提下，扩大岛民的队伍，把NPC数量从34位增加到54位；NPC不再是单纯的引路人，而是岛上的小副本和支线任务，承担发PIN的职责；最重要的是，要尝试把去年“出圈”的NPC互动模式复制到每一位NPC的身上。
项目组的成员告诉我，他们在研究了去年的互动模式后，从更加玩家有沉浸感、互动感的层面确定了今年NPC的设置。而导演组要做的则是要在大的前提下下，让所有角色都变得更加贴合世界观，设定上更加饱满，以及强化角色的演出。这种变化也对应着RED LAND区域划分上的变化：去年场地的模块划分并没有今年这么清晰，今年的不同模块都做了特别主题，所以在区域内的NPC的互动玩法和人物设定都变得和区域本身强相关。比如黄金海岸线上，所有NPC都是跟商人、金钱交易有关，再比如翻身时空港，这里被设定成多次元融合的赛博都市，所以会出现维修师、领航员、次元邮差。
很多玩家在互动的过程中了解了NPC的人设
“我们在前期会设计非常多的角色，然后不断筛选，最后呈现给玩家的是54位。整个筛选过程中最重要的是两个标准：第一，这个角色出现在这里，世界观上能不能成立。第二，他的互动玩法、角色身份，能不能给玩家带来足够的情绪价值，同时轻巧、又梗，适合用户发笔记和传播。”伞说，在整个岛民的设定、面试和培训过程中，导演组和项目组的成员都会一起来衡量这些内容。
在这个过程中，被筛选出的角色都会承担不同的功能或者情绪侧重，比如“吟游诗人”“蒙面侠盗”，都是在演绎、互动上足够丰富、会抛梗、有趣的角色，他们判断这会让玩家觉得好玩；再比如重生试炼场的“战地小护士”角色，她吸取了去年“小菜农”的成功经验——去年，小菜农会对玩家表达“你好好休息”之类的关心，也是很多玩家情感浓度最高的角色；今年，小护士同样会在现场安慰玩家，提供创可贴、冰凉贴、暖宝宝之类的补给，“这可以给一些心情不好的玩家提供情绪上的支持”。
“海鸥”是今年RED LAND很有梗的一个NPC
■ 互动
很多RED LAND的工作人员都记得，去年RED LAND最后一天的玩家欢送仪式上，演员们自发地从休息室一路走出来和玩家道别，很多NPC都哭了。当时的NPC“小菜农”在人群中找到了一位之前没有完成互动的玩家，两个人抱在一起哭，给现场的玩家和工作人员都留下了深刻印象。
“当时我发现NPC和玩家之间的情感浓度真的是很高的。”伞对我说，“我们当时其实并没有要求NPC需要特意在告别的时候做出情景演绎，很多演员都是自发性的。作为从业者，我看到都觉得很感动，所以我们也从当时的告别仪式上得到了灵感，希望在今年更加强调情绪、人设上的部分。”
今年也能在社交媒体看到，即使在活动结束后，NPC依然会自发地保持人设和玩家互动
“我们会希望可以进一步强化主角和NPC间的关系，我们会假设NPC和主角之前就是朋友，不管是互动还是做一些功能性的指引的时候都要非常热情、贴心，没有隔阂。”伞说，“去年其实也是这样的设定，但是今年会更加饱满，甚至可能最开始就给玩家一种情绪、视觉上的冲击——如果你转角忽然看到一个NPC非常激动地对你跳起来招手，那么你可能就会更愿意和她互动，可能你最开始是不想和她互动的，但是因为这种一瞬间的冲击，你愿意去和她交互。这就是我们的目的，即使不是为了NPC而来的玩家，也能在这些时候收获到一些出乎意料的情绪。”
与NPC合照的玩家
导演组成员告诉我，他们在前期对所有的NPC进行了大量的培训，这些培训包括演绎状态、台词剧本，也包括整体的世界观和交互NPC的世界观，还有大量的“他们猜测可能会遇到的问题”，每位NPC要背诵的台词超过4000字，培训手册达到6万字。
“这些台词需要大量的时间去练习，但是我们觉得是有必要的，因为不能保证每个NPC即兴都发挥得很好，那么背诵足量的文稿内容可以保证下限。”伞说，“我们的培训时间会接近一个月，到后面我们的每个NPC都能达到在原本的基础上加入自己的理解，我会对他们说，要时时刻刻都想着这个角色。”
和很多玩家一起交流的NPC
“之前接手的大部分线下活动的NPC演出培训都不会达到这种强度。”他补充，“我们到后面会有一个特殊环节，所有NPC围坐在一起，大家互相扮演玩家，提出任何刁钻的问题去提问，然后代入角色想到回答。”
他举起一个例子：岛民中的“造型师”，在最开始背台词的时候总是很痛苦，感觉一直在死记硬背，大家建议她试着就像面对朋友一样给出造型上的建议，“比如在帮忙做造型的时候，你看着玩家的眼睛，你可以夸他的眼睛，你觉得他的脊梁很挺拔，觉得他的肤色很好，不需要特别背些什么，就是发自内心地找到这些地方”。后来，在保洁阿姨上前交谈时，造型师下意识地伸出手，用梳子为阿姨整理好了刘海。
也是在去年的RED LAND上，项目组成员还发现了一个让他们意外的现象：很多来到现场的玩家真的会和NPC分享很多自己现实生活中的心事，讲述自己在现实生活中遇到的问题和困境，在漫展限定的时间里，很多玩家都似乎变得大胆起来，愿意分享很多东西。
比如，他们在某个展台附近注意到有玩家和一位NPC抱怨，“天气好热，你都不知道前面有个乙游，我排了两圈都排不到，怎么办？”，NPC安慰地摸了摸女孩的头发，说“你不要难受了，要不然我托我的岛民朋友帮你去放风？”，玩家说“不用了，我就在你这里待一会就好了，因为只有你这里不会赶我”。这个对话给他们留下了很深的印象。
“一开始我以为是演员们主动在cue这件事情，但其实不是的，甚至有一些玩家他连续来三天就找同一个人，每天都唠家常，甚至带很多小零食，然后坐在那吃，然后陪着NPC，看他互动完下一个人，然后人走之后接着唠。”伞说。这其实是一个无心之举，后来他和导演组的同事讨论，想“是不是很多玩家可能三次元没什么朋友，但其实挺需要倾诉的，因为真的会有很多烦心事”。
很多玩家和NPC之间会有意外的交互
他们觉得这种交互是非常重要的，所以在今年，很多NPC从设置上就更强调了这些情感上的连接。比如NPC中的“小邮差”，她会在大街上随机拉住玩家，递出明信片，说“有一封寄给你的信”，这些信的内容来自上一个玩家的祝福。这种互动会高度依赖现场大家的连接状态，但只要有人能写出好东西，就会变成一个很好的互动。
■ 沉浸
最近几年，很多游戏的线下活动都开始格外强调和注重提供给玩家“沉浸感”的体验。从从业者的视角来说，伞也能感受到这种明显的变化：很多活动不再只是让演员Cosplay就好，而是还需要更多演绎、互动的部分，几乎所有来线下的玩家都很需要这种有很强的情绪反馈的互动。
“这其实是在补足之前很多线下活动的短板。”伞说，“可能是因为近几年线下活动越来越多了，大家都越来越卷了，还有一个重要因素在于很多游戏展、漫展或者游戏IP的活动，开始更加注重这种有交互的、有内容的部分，这可以增加玩家的粘性，也有助于后续线上的传播。”
在RED LAND开展第一天的媒体交流会上，RED LAND核心主创、小红书游戏二次元运营负责人萤火也在交流中提到了这一点。在她看来，强化用户的“主角式互动体验”，是RED LAND提供给玩家的核心差异化体验之一。在RED LAND，几乎所有的展台都会配备自己IP的NPC和玩家互动，而在展台之外，岛民NPC则会继续强化这种互动感，最后通过每天下午的花车巡游打通IP的划分，“这是一个属于所有人的大事件”。
花车巡游是RED LAND最让人印象深刻的环节之一
“就像我们经常提到的那句‘欢迎回家，永远的主角’。即使今年有很多新角色，他其实没有见过去年的老玩家，但他们也要营造出一直把主角放在心上的感觉。我们在写词阶段，尤其写欢迎1.0玩家回归的时候，都会在设想这个场景，这个角色站在这里，看到主角回来，他自己的世界观框架下，他会说出什么样的话。”伞说。
“欢迎回家，永远的主角”是RED LAND的核心主题
“虚拟的角色，但是感情要是真实的。我们会希望能够达成这样的效果，如果玩家每年都来、每年都见到某个NPC，那么他肯定最后真的会觉得自己‘回家了’，我们希望这样的故事能够一直延续下去。”

title: Razer’s Wolverine V4 Controller Is Overkill For Most Gamers, And That’s The Point
text:
Razer has officially revealed the next entry in its line of high-end gaming controllers, the Wolverine V4 for Xbox and PC. Geared toward competitive gamers--not that there's anything stopping you from using it to play Vampire Survivors--and it focuses primarily on polling performance and thumbstick sensor architecture.
One of the biggest changes is Razer choosing capacitive contactless sensors backed by a 16-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for the thumbsticks, rather than the usual Hall Effect magnetic sensor. While Hall Effect thumbsticks are popular for their durability and for essentially eliminating stick drift, they can be prone to magnetic interference. Not a dealbreaker if you're playing at home, but in a competitive scene where victory is measured in fractions of a second, this can be an issue. In comparison, Razer is aiming to offer the same drift resistance, finer granularity, and smoother signal tracking with capacitive sensing.
Then there's the polling rate, which is absurdly high. For example, a DualSense Edge is capable of offering up to 1,000Hz (1 ms to 8 ms input latency), but the Wolverine V4 pushes that number up to 8,000Hz in both its wired and wireless configurations when used on PC, which, in theory, should put that on par with high-end esports mice and keyboards. This isn't the first Razer controller to feature an 8,000Hz polling rate, as the Wolverine V3 Pro was also equipped to reach those numbers.
Just don't expect to reach those levels on Xbox Series X|S, as hardware limitations cap the refresh rate at 250Hz, meaning the 8,000Hz benefit is strictly for PC competitive gaming.
The controller also offers four removable magnetic back buttons and two top claw-grip bumpers, with a modular magnetic design that lets players quickly swap components out, stripping the controller of unused buttons and extra weight. First-person shooter players can also use a back-mounted physical toggle switch with software-tunable actuation points, allowing them to fine-tune the hair-trigger click threshold.
That makes for a solid controller on paper, even if you don't need all of its features. The wireless model has an MSRP of $200, making it a little bit more expensive than the Xbox Elite Series 2 wireless controller and on par with the DualSense Edge (which can also be used on PC). If you'd prefer a wired option, the Wolverine V4 wired version will set you back $100.
Another controller worth keeping an eye on is the recently revealed Genki Manta . Genki launched a Kickstarter campaign for it, raising over $1.1 million for a peripheral that combines high customizability with an OLED display. The company aims to launch it next year, with an MSRP of $279.

title: Xbox Was At An “All Time Low,” But Is Now Growing Again CEO Says Without Providing Any Real Evidence
text:
During a town hall meeting today, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma spoke to staff to help reassure them following mass layoffs and studio closures related to the "reset" of the business.
Windows Central reports that Sharma told staff that Xbox is "making the right decisions" and that "after an all time low, we've started to return to growth," though she did not share any specifics. She added that Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2, and World of Warcraft: Forever had "strong" starts, though she did not share any specifics.
Sharma said, "We've started to return to growth, more than 2 to 3 times what we were, and we expect that continue." She did not share any specifics about what "2 to 3 times" actually means, though.
Sharma also told staff that Xbox's "Gen-10" platform--AKA Project Helix--will be, as rumored, a "family of devices" because "there is no one device that fits all."
She said it's important for Xbox to have a "great console first," but there will also be options for players who are "on the go." Sharma went on to say that Microsoft will manufacture some of these devices, and others Microsoft will find partners for.
"So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this," she said.
Sharma didn't get into specifics about its next console or portable devices, but they're in the works amidst a very challenging time given the AI-fueled demand for memory and components. The global macroeconomic environment that has driven up oil prices has also rocked markets. Not only this, but in the US, the Federal Reserve recently raised rates, impacting borrowing costs with the effects trickling through various market categories, including gaming.
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella praised Sharma for making such deep and extensive cuts at Xbox . This has so far included 1,600 layoffs in July , close to 300 more in September , and additional job losses to come . Microsoft also closed or divested of a number of studios, including Double Fine and Ninja Theory .
Some theorized Sharma was streamlining Xbox to make it more attractive to a prospective buyer, but she recently insisted that Xbox is not for sale . A lot of people don't believe her, though, pointing back to her comments about how "the plan's the plan until it's not the plan."
Beyond these moves, Sharma also oversaw a massive restructuring of the Xbox business that included Activision taking over the Halo series and Bethesda's remit expanding to also cover Obsidian.

title: A Scary-Looking New Conjuring Game Just Got Announced, And It’s Out Next Week On Netflix
text:
Out of nowhere, Netflix and Until Dawn developer Supermassive Games announced a new The Conjuring game, and it's out next week.
The Conjuring: Unspoken releases on October 13 through Netflix, so you don't need any dedicated hardware or controller to play it.
The game is an "interactive paranormal investigation" experience where players decide how the story progresses based on the dialogue options they choose. Players use their phone to walk through the fictional Red Lion Inn to search for clues about "things that go bump in the night," Netflix said.
You play as demonologist Francesca Noakes, and you'll use an electromagnetic field reader, an infrared camera, and spirit box to hunt for ghosts.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uSN_LlaJAXU
Netflix said you don't need to know anything about The Conjuring to enjoy Unspoken, but people familiar with the series will get "a lot more from the experience."
"There are a few familiar faces that pop up in the game, and knowing the backstory adds to the overall impact," Netflix said.
Unspoken will be available on Netflix on October 13. It was made in partnership with Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment, whose parent company, Warner Bros. Discovery, was just acquired by Paramount/Skydance .

title: GTA 6 Will Not Stream To PC Through Xbox, Despite Earlier Report
text:
PC players hoping to find a way to play GTA 6 when it launches on consoles next month must be feeling pretty disappointed, as Microsoft has clarified that Grand Theft Auto 6 will not be available to stream to PC via Xbox Cloud Gaming. The news follows an earlier report claiming Xbox had secured exclusive streaming rights to Rockstar's highly anticipated game.
The clarification came from Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball, who addressed The Verge 's report. Ball said the excitement surrounding GTA 6 and Xbox had resulted in some inaccurate reporting.
His full statement read, "While the excitement for GTA 6 and Xbox is great to see, it has also led to some misreporting. We are looking forward to launching GTA 6 on Xbox November 19, though the game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC."
That means, sadly for PC players, that you shouldn't expect to fire up Xbox Cloud Gaming on November 19 and find yourself wandering around Vice City without a console.
https://twitter.com/ballmatthew/status/2107667069797802443?s=20
The original report from The Verge claimed that Microsoft had secured exclusive game-streaming rights for GTA 6, citing sources familiar with the company's plans. The report followed comments from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who apparently told employees that Microsoft was preparing to do something with GTA 6 that "no other platform holder is doing."
The report suggested the arrangement could have been significant for PC players, who as of yet don't know when they'll be able to get their hands on the game.
Rockstar has yet to announce a PC version of GTA 6, which is officially confirmed for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. A streaming arrangement could have offered PC players a way to play the game at launch without waiting for the GTA 6 PC release date.
The confusion arrives at a pretty interesting time for Xbox Cloud Gaming. Microsoft is making significant changes to the service in November, including introducing a pay-as-you-go option and changing the amount of cloud gaming time available across Game Pass tiers.

title: Resident Evil Requiem DLC Could Further Rewrite One Of The Series’ Biggest Villains
text:
Resident Evil Requiem is one of this year's biggest hits, and Capcom plans to build on that success with new story DLC. While it hasn't yet revealed when it'll be out or what it's about, one of the game's writers, Haris Orkin, recently teased that the DLC will shed new light on Oswell E. Spencer , one of the biggest villains in the Resident Evil series.
"I think villains honestly are really fun to write, because I usually see every villain as a hero of their own story. So the villain is like in their mind they're a hero," Orkin said in an interview with the Distance Nerding podcast. I mean, Victor Gideon thinks he's going to save the world in Requiem. We have an arc for Spencer in Requiem. "Where you understand that more. And then in the DLC you will understand that even further. I probably shouldn't say that, but yeah."
https://youtu.be/gaTmFHQdLlo
Resident Evil Requiem spoilers below
Compared to his appearances in previous Resident Evil games, Oswell E. Spencer is more sympathetic, harboring genuine regret for his role in establishing the Umbrella Corporation, his research on the Progenitor Virus, and his ambitious goal of remaking the world with his bioweapons. As revealed in Requiem-- and spoilers if you haven't played it yet --Spencer adopted a baby girl called Grace in 2001, and he successfully developed the powerful antiviral Elpis so that he could eliminate all Progenitor-based viral weapons, as part of his mission to atone for his sins.
That version of Spencer is narratively at odds with the version we see in Resident Evil 5, as before his death in 2006 at the hands of Albert Wesker, he was a bit of a bastard who apparently still harbored delusions of grandeur and had started work on a new virus to help him become immortal.
Then again, Capcom has been rewriting Resident Evil lore with its remakes, and this new version of Spencer is arguably more fascinating than a stereotypical mustache-twirling villain. While we don't know if Capcom plans to eventually make Resident Evil 5--one of the more controversial entries in the series--it'll be interesting to see if Spencer succumbs to his ambitions once again before Wesker finishes him off.
Since its launch, Capcom has updated Resident Evil Requiem with some photography tools and a new "Leon Must Die" mode. Resident Evil producer Jun Takeuchi also spoke about the meaning behind the title, adding to the confusion . Following the blockbuster success of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, the next entry in the video game series is out soon. The remake of Resident Evil: Code Veronica launches in 2027.

title: Skydance Is Merging Paramount And Warner Bros.’ Game Studios Into One Unit
text:
With Paramount's $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery in the bag, details on what this merger means for the Warner Bros. game division have finally been revealed. Warner Bros. Interactive will merge with the newly formed Paramount Games Studio, and it'll oversee projects based on Skydance's rich--and newly acquired-library of IP. That lineup includes Avatar: The Last Airbender, South Park, Mortal Kombat, Game of Thrones, and Star Trek--and that's not even mentioning the treasure trove of DC Comics IP that the company now owns.
The new division will be overseen by Tony Driscoll, president of games and experiences at Skydance, and one of the executives leading corporate strategy and development at the company. Driscoll had previously described video games as a "core pillar" of entertainment, alongside film and TV.
SpongeBob Mortal Kombat crossover when?
"We’re investing in our future growth engines alongside our core ambitions in TV, film and direct-to-consumer: Games, experiences, consumer products, and publishing," Gordon wrote in a staff memo (via Variety ). "These are core pillars of our strategy to build engagement and fandom in both the physical and digital worlds. We want to meet consumers where they watch, play, and engage."
It's still unclear what the future plans are for the growing Skydance gaming division, or how hard it'll be hit by looming layoffs. This branch of Skydance will now be the home to some big WBI developers like Avalanche Software (Hogwarts Legacy), NetherRealm Studios (Mortal Kombat), Rocksteady Studios (Batman: Arkham Series and one Suicide Squad game I don't want to talk about), and TT Games (Various Lego games).
Former Activision CEO Bobby Kotick has also joined the board of directors, and Skydance is also producing the Call of Duty movie with Activision , which is scheduled to hit theaters in 2028.

title: State Of Decay 3 Was Announced Early To Keep Undead Labs On Microsoft’s Radar
text:
After leaving the Xbox Game Studios portfolio, State of Decay 3 developer Undead Labs is now an independent, employee-owned studio. The developer had previously announced State of Decay 3 all the way back in 2020--partly to keep the project and the studio on Microsoft's radar--as the company embarked on an acquisition spree. Now one of several departures from Microsoft's gaming division following the bloody " Xbox reset " that has seen scores of jobs slashed throughout 2026, Undead Labs also had to cut staff as it entered a new era. But was there any behind-the-scenes drama that led to its exit from Xbox?
Speaking to The Game Business , studio boss Philip Holt said that ultimately, nothing went wrong. It was more a case of reading the room and making a proposal to Microsoft that the company accepted. "It was an accelerated period of time for Microsoft's divestiture," Holt explained. "We had a lot of interest. I also thought that because we were so close to being in revenue, the amount of capital that we needed to finish [State of Decay 3] was not an insurmountable amount that we couldn't go raise it ourselves. I knew other studios were doing management buyouts, so I submitted an offer for a management-led acquisition, and Microsoft thought that would be a good idea."
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c5--CgCpM7M
Holt also addressed why State of Decay 3 was originally announced so far in advance, as in the eight years that it was under the Xbox umbrella, it never released a single game--but it did drop 38 updates for the popular State of Decay 2. He explained that a small team had been working on the game since 2020--with development picking up a few years later--and that announcing the game so early helped the studio avoid being lost in the shuffle during Xbox's buying spree of publishers like Bethesda and Activision Blizzard.
"I didn’t think Microsoft was done being acquisitive, and I didn't think they'd continue buying small developers; I assumed they'd start buying big things. I was a little worried about getting swallowed up or divested before we had a chance to present to the world what we were working on. So, it was a bit of a marker on the table. I was saying, State of Decay 3, we're announcing it, the audience knows it’s in development, and here’s a trailer to demonstrate our vision."
State of Decay 3 will still launch day-one through Game Pass, and Holt credited the subscription service with helping the horror franchise reach 25 million players. He also said that becoming an independent studio allowed Undead Labs to focus on serving an audience and being profitable. "We need to make a profit, we need to be sustainable, we need to pay ourselves and our partners--and it is a goal. This is not a charity. But it’s not the number-one most important objective."
Undead Labs joins Double Fine and Compulsion Games as former Xbox studios, but the future of Hellblade and DmC: Devil May Cry developer Ninja Theory is looking grim. After deals to acquire the studio fell through, it looks like the studio will soon be shut down .

title: GTA 6 Won’t Make You “All-Powerful” Like GTA 5 Did
text:
Rockstar boss Rob Nelson has stated that GTA 6 won't make players "all-powerful" like they were in GTA 5 and the games that came before it. For GTA 6, this means NPCs in the world will have impulses of their own, and could come after you.
Speaking to IGN , Nelson said, "The world will act upon you as well as you acting upon the world." In previous GTA games, except for the police, the player was the only one with an "invisible arsenal hidden away," and everyone in the world would run away in terror. "This world in GTA 6 is not like that," he said.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_vlzIPpyJR0
Nelson went on to say that GTA 6's story, which follows the partners in crime and lovers Jason and Lucia, is about "criminals on the run." However, the game's narrative is such that they are incentized to "do what they need to do while not drawing unnecessary attention."
"So if you're doing things on a mission that you are required to do--or you’re robbing places, or somebody comes and messes with you and you have to deal with them by smacking them down or whatever--that’s all fair game," he said. "It's when you go beyond what is necessary on a consistent basis or you do completely unnecessary stuff consistently that you may start to sway your criminal profile in a certain direction. Maybe you care about that as a player, maybe you don't. There is no right or wrong way to play this."
Nelson said being "overpowered" as a character compared to everyone else except the cops "can be fun but not as fun" as a world in which other people may have "impulses of their own and act upon you."
"You are still powerful and capable, but you are not the only one capable of violence or the only one with weapons or the only crazy person out there," he said. "It makes the world far more unpredictable and interesting. It's something that we started doing in Red Dead Redemption 2, where you are not the only dangerous person in the world. There are gangs that will attack you, things that will happen to you. The world will act upon you. That happens here a lot, and then when it does, you have a decision to make. How do you want to deal with it?"
In GTA 6, the cops are getting upgrades, too. A new "heat" system means the police now know what the player looks like and what they're wearing, so even if players put on a hat or glasses, the cops still know who they are until they change clothes.
GTA 6 releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it's reportedly already sold close to 6 million copies. A recent report said the game might be available to stream in November, but that's apparently not the case .

title: Google Playground Wants Everyone To Make AI Games, And Maybe Everyone Shouldn’t
text:
Stadia might be dead , but Google isn't giving up on gaming. The company has rolled out Playground , a platform built around AI that "lets you create, play, and share custom games." It's browser-based and labeled as an "experiment" to start. There's also Unity Spark support, which will offer more development options for people who catch the creator bug.
Google's pitch claims that this new platform makes game creation more democratic by ending gatekeeping to development. The company states that Playground "lowers the barriers to creation, so bringing game ideas to life can now be as easy as describing it through a few prompts--no coding experience required." The platform also feels like the company's attempt at taking a piece of the Roblox pie--something that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reportedly wants with Minecraft , too.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dxvrvfyicp0
However, the initial rollout feels pretty underwhelming. The most hilarious part of the Playground experience, so far, is realizing how misleading the cover art for games is after actually playing them. For example, we checked out Volcano Run. The key image shows a sports car racing around a road crumbling; meanwhile, the actual gameplay is a rudimentary rectangular motorcycle (we think) driving in a Tron-like environment.
One of the Unity Spark highlights is called Horror Story, and the game starts with players following a ghost into a haunted house. How that ghost shuffles into the residence is one of the funnier animations we've witnessed in a game recently.
The most promising experience we checked out was Steampunk Match, a match-3 puzzle game. Players need to create combos to stop a boiler from exploding. This game felt much better than others that attempted to take a swing at the action-RPG genre, such as Catacombs.
If you are looking to make your own game for Playground, that opportunity is apparently rolling out to people "soon." However, Google says people can upgrade their Google One plan to get started immediately.

title: The Next Gears Of War Game Probably Won’t Need 7 Years To Cook
text:
After a lengthy hiatus, Gears of War returned this week to Xbox Series X|S and PC with a new adventure set during the cataclysmic events of Emergence Day. For fans of the series, it has been a long wait, as the previous entry in the series, Gears 5 , was released all the way back in 2019. Will there be another seven-year stretch between new Gears games? Gears of War: E-Day developer The Coalition doesn't think so, as the new game lays the groundwork for a quicker turnaround for new potential chapters in the IP.
Speaking to the BBC , Coalition studio head Mike Crump said that E-Day provides a "great foundation" for future games, and he claimed that "the next game will not take nearly as long" to make. "What I say to myself, what I say to the team, is we just we need to focus on the things that we can control. For us that's about shipping a great game that people are going to love and I feel like, as a team, we've done that," Crump added in response to questions about the safety of the studio and its institutional knowledge during a period of mass layoffs at Xbox. "We've got a great team here. And the leadership team in particular has worked together for upwards of 20 years. So there's definitely a continuity of knowledge and experience."
So far, The Coalition appears to have been spared the brunt of " Xbox reset " layoffs, but fears remain that the axe might swing their way now that Gears of War: E-Day has launched.
Recent changes at Xbox have seen several studios consolidated under Bethesda and Activision, and even Xbox's high-profile Halo series has not been spared. After being under the remit of Halo Studios for several years, a new team at Activision is now developing the next Halo game, rumored to be a new division within Call of Duty developer Sledgehammer Games.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=teClq4qYyzQ
The future of the Gears of War series likely rests with its commercial performance, but as an Xbox exclusive, there's only so much room for sales before you factor in its availability as a day-one Xbox Game Pass release and its launch during a crowded period on the gaming calendar. Crump sees things differently, believing the true measure of E-Day's success will be its ability to move the needle for Xbox and show what the gaming brand is capable of as it enters a new era, not just sales numbers.
"We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to its limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware," Crump said.
