旧南方已成焦土
旧南方已成焦土，但传奇未死，亦非生者。《末世神枪（Guns of Eschaton）》是一款类魂FPS游戏，背景设定于末世西部。洞悉猎杀你的怪物，精打细算每一发子弹，用火药与祷文锻造独属于你的战斗风格。无论是单枪匹马还是并肩作战，向西而行吧，枪客，与这片沉沦的国度共赴终局。游戏将登陆PS5、XBOX Series及PC平台，具体发售日期待定，试玩Demo现已在PC平台推出。

title: Switch 2版《剑星》宣传视频
text:
揭开地球衰败之谜
在后末日动作冒险游戏《剑星》中拯救濒临灭绝的人类。揭开地球衰败之谜，体验激烈战斗与曲折剧情。现在你无论在家中还是旅途中，均可体验伊芙的旅程，并可使用Joy-Con 2的陀螺仪控制钓鱼等活动。游戏将于11月5日登陆Switch 2平台。

title: 《战地风云6》第五赛季实机预告
text:
一切都将重新洗牌
当《战地风云6》第五赛季于10月13日登陆拉斯维加斯时，一切都将重新洗牌。赛季期间，在三张新地图上战斗，包括拉斯维加斯大道和51区，从赌场和屋顶到开阔沙漠和秘密地下隧道。用六种新武器和两款新载具扩充你的军械库，挑战「豪赌行动」，攀登多人模式排行榜，组建小队，并重返更新后的布莱克韦尔油田和新索贝克城。此外，大逃杀排位赛将正式上线，并同期推出公开系列赛。然后，在限时万圣节活动中，面对更险恶的存在。庄家总是通吃，向来如此。

title: 《战锤40K：爆矢枪2》「瓦什托尔」预告
text:
以帝皇之名消灭叛军
在《战锤40K：爆矢枪2（Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2）》中以帝皇之名消灭叛军！体验复古第一人称射击游戏《战锤40K：爆矢枪》的续作，扮演极限战士马鲁姆·凯多或战斗修女奈拉·维拉思，迎战更多敌人，尝试更多武器，探索新的净化方式！游戏将于10月14日登陆PS5、XBOX Series及PC平台。

title: 《战锤幸存者》发售日预告
text:
消灭无尽的敌人浪潮
《战锤幸存者（Warhammer Survivors）》是一款快节奏的Roguelite幸存者游戏，扮演来自《战锤40K》和《战锤：西格玛时代》中的角色，收集并进化标志性武器，消灭无尽的敌人浪潮。游戏由《战锤40K：爆矢枪》的开发商Auroch Digital与《吸血鬼幸存者》的开发商poncle合作打造，将于11月10日登陆PS5、XBOX Series、Switch、Switch 2、PC、iOS及安卓平台。

title: 《星球大战：银河赛车手》发售宣传视频
text:
在混乱中一决高下
《星球大战：银河赛车手（Star Wars: Galactic Racer）》是一款以竞速为核心的惊险赛车游戏，以星球大战星系的法外之地外环星域为游戏背景。帝国覆灭之后，银河系得到了重建，银河联赛也应运而生：这是一个未经官方认可的地下赛车联盟，在各大财团的资金支持下，飞行员会在混乱中一决高下，争夺冠军。游戏现已登陆PS5、XBOX Series及PC平台。

title: 《战锤40K：黑暗异端》侦探系统预告
text:
以审判官侍仆的身份开始服役吧
置身战锤40K宇宙观构筑的黑暗未来，玩家将扮演残酷无情的秩序维护者。以审判官侍仆的身份开始服役吧，你将在细节丰满的剧情世界中调查异端邪说，统御各怀绝技的队员，左右卡利西斯星区的未来轨迹。每个抉择都重若千钧，正义早已荡然无存，救赎与湮灭仅隔瞬息之距。深入帝国审判庭的权力核心，感受其庞然伟力，亲历错综的权力网络、官僚迷局与惊心动魄的派系斗争。《战锤40K：黑暗异端（Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy）》将登陆PS5、XBOX Series及PC平台，具体发售日期待定。

title: 《黎明杀机》×《尼尔：自动人形》联动宣传视频
text:
万物皆为消亡而生
万物皆为消亡而生...迷雾之中尤为如此。经典游戏角色重获新生，在恶灵的试炼中寻找全新的使命。《黎明杀机》「尼尔：自动人形」收藏为凤敏、木村唯、军团推出全新套装，化身2B、A2与艾米尔。

title: 《渊舟蚀影》试玩Demo宣传视频
text:
与潜伏在水下和陆地上的可怖怪物战斗
《渊舟蚀影（Dreadmoor）》是一款黑暗风格的第一人称钓鱼冒险游戏，以一个因昔日灾难而被淹没、逐渐腐朽的世界为背景。在浑浊的水域垂钓，升级你的船只，制作生存装备，与潜伏在水下和陆地上的可怖怪物战斗。试玩Demo现已在Steam平台上线。

title: 《战锤幸存者》试玩Demo实机演示
text:
将于11月10日发售
《战锤幸存者（Warhammer Survivors）》是一款快节奏的Roguelite幸存者游戏，扮演来自《战锤40K》和《战锤：西格玛时代》中的角色，收集并进化标志性武器，消灭无尽的敌人浪潮。游戏由《战锤40K：爆矢枪》的开发商Auroch Digital与《吸血鬼幸存者》的开发商poncle合作打造，将于11月10日登陆PS5、XBOX Series、Switch、Switch 2、PC、iOS及安卓平台。

title: 《高达 异轨征途》游戏概览预告
text:
能体验高速自在的高机动战斗的动作游戏
《高达 异轨征途》是能体验高速自在的高机动战斗的动作游戏。玩家将化身螺旋高达驾驶「雷克斯」，和搭档哈啰「惟」一起挺身面对未知敌人带来的威胁。舞台是使用照片级写实表现精致的广大宇宙，描绘左右人类未来的壮阔故事。崭新的高达体验，自此开始。游戏将于2027年3月5日登陆PS5、XBOX Series及PC平台。

title: 《猫壳机动队》试玩Demo宣传视频
text:
选择你的猫咪驾驶员
《猫壳机动队》是一款以机甲组装为核心的构筑向肉鸽自走棋。选择你的猫咪驾驶员，搭配装备与模块，打造专属机甲，挑战异步PvP对战、剧情模式、与PvE远征，并在模拟实验室中测试和分享你的构筑方案。游戏将于2027年1月20日在Steam平台开启抢先体验，试玩Demo现已上线。

title: NOVA海外独立游戏见闻 Vol.155
text:
Vol.155（10 月第 1 周）
本期见闻覆盖时间：9 月 28 日至 10 月 4 日
本期整理： Alonso
行业见闻录
独立游戏开发者遭勒索，被威胁抢先发售游戏“克隆版”
上周，多名独立游戏开发者收到同一手法的勒索邮件：发件人威胁称，若不在 24 小时内送出价值 200 美元的 Steam 物品，自己就会盗版其正在开发的游戏并抢先发售。 海外媒体 InTheIndie 首先报道了此事 。
最早公开这封勒索邮件的是《Iron Pilgrim》的开发者 Weasel Pit，该游戏计划于 2027 年登陆 Steam。发件人自称 Zagir Harif，声称看中了该项目的创意，并附上一段疑似由 AI 根据该游戏宣发物料生成的仿冒视频。 另一家工作室 Psicodart Games 也表示收到同一发件人的邮件 ，对方威胁要盗版其正在开发的作品《Circusar》并抢先发售。
Psicodart Games 收到的勒索邮件内容 /图片：Twi/X: @PsicodartGames
不过，有网友发现，Weasel Pit 自己此前也曾发出过类似威胁，因此怀疑他在自导自演。事情经过是，一名开发者曾在 Reddit 上分享了一个“从 35000 株三叶草中找出 1 株四叶草”的游戏构想。Weasel Pit 锐评这类机制是“偷懒的游戏”，并扬言如果对方真把它上架 Steam，他就做个免费版一并上架。
对此，Weasel Pit 发表声明：他承认自己在 Reddit 上发布那条留言是错误的，并已向那位开发者道歉；但他强调，索要 200 美元的勒索邮件并非只发给他一人，其他开发者也收到了同样的邮件，因此这件事并非他自导自演。
Weasel Pit 的游戏《Iron Pilgrim》
Steam 的“折扣与推荐”页面将由算法完全驱动
9 月 30 日， Valve 宣布将调整 Steam"折扣与活动"标签页的运作方式 ，从人工日历排期改为面向每位用户的动态个性化推荐。
Valve 表示，该页面今后由 Steam 算法挑选游戏，不再依赖人工，预计更多游戏将获得展示机会。目前，该页面的游戏要么由 Valve 员工手动排期，要么由合作方通过 Steamworks 自行排期。过去几个月，Valve 测试用动态个性化推荐替换部分策展位；结果显示，该板块单日展示的游戏数量增至原来的 10 倍，商店页面访问量、愿望单添加量和加购量均明显增长。
Valve 已暂停该页面的策展位排期，但已排期的开发者仍保留原有档期。Valve 表示将在未来数周公布更多安排，并计划在 2027 年初彻底停用人工日历。Valve 还将推出新工具，帮助开发者管理折扣与促销活动，从而“让开发者专注打磨游戏，而不必花时间去说服 Valve 推荐自己的产品”。
图片： Valve
须田刚一脱离网易，重归独立
9 月 30 日，《英雄不再》《Killer7》开发商 Grasshopper Manufacture 宣布脱离母公司网易游戏，重新成为独立工作室。 工作室创始人兼 CEO 须田刚一（Suda51）在 X 上公布了这一消息 。
网易游戏于 2021 年收购该工作室。须田刚一表示，团队完成新作《Romeo is a Dead Man》后开始考虑下一步方向，产生了“向全世界玩家呈现风格更加多样的作品”的强烈愿望，并称决定是“与网易游戏充分讨论、在对方慷慨配合下”做出的。他还表示，无论发行方式如何，都会坚持打造带有 Grasshopper 特色的“NO GAME NO LIFE”体验。
近年，网易持续收缩海外投资：2025 年 9 月关闭财报尚可的 T-Minus Zero，2026 年 3 月停止资助名越稔洋工作室的《Gang of Dragon》。此外，Grasshopper 的最新作品《Romeo is a Dead Man》的销量尚未公布。
Grasshopper Manufature Independent Again. /图片：X@Suda51
《王权》开发商 Nerial 宣布进入“休眠状态”
10 月 1 日，《王权》《Card Shark》开发商 Nerial 宣布，在与母公司 Devolver Digital 商议后，工作室将终止所有游戏开发，并进入“休眠状态”。
CEO Tamara Alliot 与创意总监 François Alliot 在社交媒体发布的联合信中称 ，“我们与 Devolver 共同决定终止工作室的开发工作”。两人未说明关闭的具体原因，只表示在掌舵 13 年后需要做出改变。Tamara Alliot 在领英上列出受影响的员工及其岗位，涵盖叙事与写作、艺术指导、主程序、程序、高级程序、QA 主管、高级制作人等，并呼吁同行聘用他们。François Alliot 则表示自己将"回归纯粹独立开发者"的身份。
此举或与母公司 Devolver 的财务状况有关。今年 8 月，Devolver 管理层向股东表示，希望在经历行业“剧烈动荡期”后，停止在伦敦证券交易所的交易。
工作室 CEO 与创意总监发布的联合信
“死因推理游戏”已经自成品类
10 月 4 日， 日媒 Automaton 刊文称 ，“死因推理游戏”正形成一股潮流。这类游戏以判定死者死因为核心，玩家与开发者数量双双增加，逐渐发展成一个品类。
这一品类的源头通常可以追溯到《奥伯拉丁的回归》。玩家在该游戏中需要确认 1803 年失踪的“奥伯拉丁号”船员身份与死因，因此这类作品也被称为“类奥伯拉丁”。此后，《金偶像谜案》《金偶像崛起》凭借 2D 场景结合死因推理与叙事走红；《鲁特里一家死了》则让玩家根据资料搭建死者族谱，同样受到欢迎。更早的源头，则常上溯到《她的故事》等作品。
网页游戏《Type Help》引入了“以文字输入指认人物、场景与行动”的新机制。玩家需要为这些内容编号，再从编号中找出规律，输入新编号以换取信息。该游戏凭免费与新意催生了新潮流。受其影响，面向新手的《死亡游戏调查报告》与融入奇幻风格的《欢迎来到公会探求团！》相继推出；将《Type Help》重制为视觉小说的《加利宅邸悬案》也获得好评。
Automaton 指出，此类游戏文本量大，且与系统深度绑定，本地化难度高。若出现品质过硬的多语言作品，有望在世界范围掀起更大浪潮。
《欢迎来到公会探求团！》
《星露谷物语》1.7 更新放出三条神秘线索
新闻拾遗。 据外媒上周报道 ，《星露谷物语》作者 ConcernedApe 在该作官方 Discord 频道放出三句神秘短语，为 1.7 版本更新勾勒方向。三句话分别为“两条路线将得到延长”“三者将变成四者”“美人鱼的果实将重获自由”；除此之外再无说明，解读完全交由玩家。
围绕第一句，有人猜克林特与桑迪的剧情会扩展，也有人认为指的是社区中心与 Joja 超市两条主线。第二句较流行的解读是：镇上的孩童将从三名变成四名——目前有贾斯、雷欧与文森特三人。第三句较为费解，“美人鱼的果实”被不少玩家与农场主的孩子联系起来，推测孩子或许能长大、离开农舍去过自己的日子。以上均属玩家猜测，作者本人始终没有表态。
《星露谷物语》上市已满十年。ConcernedApe 近年专注新作开发，本作的更新节奏随之放缓，但 1.7 仍在推进。上一个大型版本 1.6 的开发前后超过三年，直到 2024 年才推出；1.7 何时落地目前仍未可知。
独游公告板
一周拾遗 ：本周值得关注的新发售、重新上架或公布新版本的独立游戏。
1. 9 月 27 日，外媒 RPS 介绍了上周发行的新作《Video Game Menu: The Game》。该作由 Sebastian Gioseffi 开发，不含任何关卡与战斗，全部内容围绕游戏的设置菜单展开：玩家在各级菜单之间切换、点按按钮，观察各项设置生效后的效果。菜单选项既有画质、垂直同步、帧数上限、亮度等常规项，也有一批非常规设置，例如将屏幕整体旋转、开启“摘下眼镜”令画面变模糊、打开“飞机模式”在画面上叠加驾驶舱图像，以及让按钮躲避光标、让文字随光标接近而缩小等。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3949620/Video_Game_Menu_The_Game/
开发追踪： 本周更新开发关键节点、尚处在开发早期或中期的独立游戏。
1. 9 月 29 日，Strange Scaffold 公布整理模拟新作《Something is Wrong with the Library》，预计 2026 年第四季度上线 Steam，由该工作室与 Frosty Pop 发行。游戏舞台是山区小镇甜榆镇的公共图书馆：亿万富翁亚历克斯·迪特尔为“净化”小镇接连杀害无家可归者，把尸体砌进图书馆的墙中。图书馆因而被灵异力量盘踞，书籍散落一地。玩家要在前任主管菲利普·谢德的协助下，用一夜时间打扫、整理图书馆，揭开共犯者的故事。馆内藏有数千本真实书名的图书，可按杜威十进分类法、作者名与书名归位；“模块化混乱系统”让每次游玩待整理的书籍组合都不相同。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3971340/Something_is_Wrong_with_the_Library/
2. 9 月 30 日，加拿大开发者 Denis Morozov 与阿尔巴尼亚作家 Milha Vek 宣布，双方共同制作的游戏《乖孩子会祷告》（Good Children Say Grace）将于 10 月 16 日上线 Steam。这是一款以 1980 年代东欧孤岛为舞台的心理恐怖冒险游戏：主角马丁因女友失踪而逐渐崩溃，父母还收养了一个烧掉自己家的同龄女孩，到后来，他眼中所见的一切都成了“蛋”。
玩家以第一人称在 3D 空间探索，并在 2.5D 场景之间切换；对话内容与行走路线都会被视作选择，最终分支出 15 种以上结局。画面为漫画式黑白并点缀红与粉，灵感取自浅野一二〇的《晚安，布布》与久米田康治的《再见！绝望先生》；配音由《玲音》的清水香里担任。
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3881920/Good_Children_Say_Grace/
3. 10 月 2 日，Springloaded 创始人 James Barnard 在接受采访时宣布，新作《Let's Build a Dungeon》将于 2027 年 2 月 11 日进入抢先体验。
玩家在其中身兼游戏工作室的老板与设计师：一边开挖地下城、布置怪物与陷阱、设计任务，看虚拟玩家游玩；一边招人、管钱、应付投资人与媒体，还要带员工赶展会。游戏内置仿 Steam 商店页与 SteamSpy 式的数据，要在数百款虚构游戏中竞争，靠愿望单、点击率与转化率看成绩；做游戏的电脑也会随年代升级，CGA 换到 VGA，配乐随声卡改变。此外还会遭黑客入侵勒索，母亲发消息催你吃饭、寄来馅饼配方等等事件。当然，馅饼也能做进游戏。

近期会员发布的一些开发日志，其中有一些会经过选择在 indienova 文章区直接发布，就不重复列出了。（因为开发日志较多，所以今后就只选取部分了，更多的请大家随时关注 indienova 的日志栏目）
标题：失忆纪元：一个绕过 LLM 长记忆瓶颈的 AI 叙事实验
来自： Nova-5vI7
作者引语： 这不是一个 AI 对话 Demo。
这是一个 AI 叙事实验。区别在于：AI 对话 Demo 里，AI 只负责把写好的剧情演出来；而这个 Demo 里，AI 根据当前世界状态，自己推导 NPC 想说什么、想做什么、会给玩家什么任务。叙事不是写好的，是从状态和性格里长出来的。
当前生成式叙事无法落地的核心瓶颈，不是 AI 写不出好台词，而是 LLM 的长期记忆不可靠。对话越长，角色信息越容易被淹没；固定上下文窗口无法维持长期一致性；LLM 经常混淆不同角色的状态。结果就是叙事碎片化、角色崩坏。
我的思路是：不让 AI 记，让世界记。

【招募美术】军事卡牌游戏《压力前线》寻画师合作，近未来+二战魔改风格，有 Demo 可玩
来自： 综合讨论组
会员： kriegsmarine
关于项目
《压力前线》是一款 1v1 军事卡牌对战游戏。核心机制：三条阵线调度、动态揭示（部署隐藏，行动后揭示）、压力值系统（挨打也是资源）。
世界观：近未来，全球金属枯竭，所有现役装备都是二战老库存反复拆解、焊接现代配件后的“拼装版本”。坦克还是 1943 年的底盘，但炮塔上焊了反应装甲、装了新式瞄具——老装备焊新科技，形成独特的“超级拼装”视觉风格。具体详情风格如附图所示。
目前进度：
· 140+张卡牌设计完成（美、德、英、苏、日本等阵营）
· 完整规则文档和卡牌数据
· 可运行 Demo（PC/移动双端可玩，有玩家测试群）
· 程序、主策已到位
需要什么
美术。主美目前的底子是硬边黑白稿（版画感）。我们需要延续这种高对比度的硬核版画质感，后续上色细化也需与此基调不违和。欢迎尝试其他技法与版画风的碰撞。目前稿子少无重改成本，风格怎么定，等你来聊。
工作内容
卡牌插画（约 140 张，分批做，不会一次压给你）、UI 视觉、对战特效、卡牌框等。先从几张概念图开始，甚至先试一张，双方都觉得合适再继续。
合作方式
项目处于早期阶段，暂无固定预算。上线后按约定比例分成，若未来有收入会优先补偿核心成员。不要求全职，按你自己的节奏来，每周有稳定产出即可（具体节奏可商量）。可以先试稿一张，通过后详谈。
联系方式
加 Q： 206775714 （请备注：美术应聘）
加 Q 后我会先发 Demo 和现有稿子给你看，你判断是否感兴趣，再决定要不要试稿。
如果你对军事题材感兴趣，或者想参与一个已经有完整设计的卡牌项目，欢迎来聊聊。

title: Warhorse co-founder believes 'AI is not a get out of jail free card' and that execs have a 'simplified mental model' of what it means for games
text:
Few things are constant in life, but the reminder that AI is wriggling its way into just about every facet of life is unfortunately pervasive. Take games for example, it's wormed its way into voice acting , voice acting , and more voice acting. But aside from giving players a plethora of dull and generic quips it's also been cited as one of the reasons behind the seemingly neverending string of layoffs in the industry.
The thought process is 'why pay humans to do work when you can pay robots to do it, just kind of worse.' This is where Warhorse's co-founder, Martin Klima, thinks videogame execs are getting it wrong, because "AI is not a get out of jail free card."
(Image credit: Future) While Klima does believe that AI may become unavoidable if cost-saving stays as important as it already is, he points out that "it doesn't work how people imagine in a very simplified mental model".
The idea that you can lay off half your staff and replace them with AI is a "fundamentally flawed idea, because it doesn't work like that". Klima believes that instead of replacing half of a team of devs, player demand for bigger and bigger games will invariably drive studios to keep their human dev teams the same size, but augmented by AI. This would, he says, allow them to make even bigger games than they could beforehand. The game that offers players more "is going to be better".
"It can mean [the game] has more branching classes," Klima adds. "It can mean it has more missions to play, whatever—people will still want to have this bigger game." While AI may not reduce the cost of the game, it will allow us to create bigger games for the same cost".
Some studios have been using machine learning to cut out busy work that only bogs its developers down for a while now, like Warcraft . Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick also commented on the tech, saying that, while AI isn't in the business of making hits because "clones don't sell", it can still be helpful to devs . Unfortunately, it looks like not everyone's got the memo just yet.

title: I've added scams to GTA 5, but I might have scammed myself
text:
Los Santos Customs
I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .
A shift in the fabric of reality: I launch Grand Theft Auto 5 and, following the now-customary hitch-and-stutter loading screen that can last anywhere from 10 seconds to five minutes, Franklin spawns into his familiar void apartment. Within seconds, he begins plummeting, screaming.
All of this is fine and normal.
But something new: Franklin carries a duffel bag with him into the abyss now, and I am unsure as to why. My guess is that it is a byproduct of my newly installed mod, ScamV , which "turns Los Santos into your digital playground." Let the possibilities unfurl ahead of you—"Take on the role of a cyber-criminal, exploit vulnerabilities, use cloned cards, and build your underground fortune."
Mostly, though, it has given me a bag. Don't get me wrong, I am sure that all of these things would be present in a regular installation of ScamV, but unfortunately ScamV in my world is forced to compete with an armageddon of other mods: the flying cars, new interiors, deleted exteriors, credit ratings and so on.
Franklin, humiliated by his failure to bank, departs. (Image credit: Rockstar) So mostly it is a bag. But wait, there is also this—the possibility of walking into a bank, any bank, and interacting with the teller by paying in fake cheques. "You don't have any fake cheques," the game tells me when I attempt this. It does not tell me where or how to obtain them. Kafka-esque. Five stars.

title: Gears of War: E-Day review — terrific shooting buoys a sluggish campaign
text:
Need to know
What is it? A prequel to the classic third-person cover shooters
Release date: October 6, 2026
Expect to pay: $70/£60
Developer: The Coalition
Publisher: Xbox Game Studios
Reviewed on: Asus ROG Zephyrus G14
Steam Deck: TBA
Link: Official site
What's the most stunning revelation in this Gears of War prequel? Marcus Fenix used to have a jump button. Yes, the king of cover-based shooting, a man more rooted to the ground than a scarecrow, spent his youth jumping to some bits of cover. So E-Day contains at least one literal leap forward for the franchise. Shame it's trapped in a slog of a campaign that's otherwise anything but.
But before I moan about that, plenty of good news first. Gears has never felt better to play. These third-person cover shooters have always been a blast when they're working, and a miserable swearing fit when you dodge roll into certain death instead of snapping into cover like you wanted to. Again.
That nonsense has finally been excised, mostly, thanks to slightly more acrobatic characters and some wise button remapping. It's amazing what a difference sticking run on L3 and giving climb its own designated button makes.
Gears of War's biggest haters are liable to characterise its cover-shooting as a dull game of whack-a-mole. Perhaps on Normal difficulty, but Hardcore is where the experience sings. Here, staying in the same spot of cover is rightfully punished. You've got to keep gaining better ground, constantly weighing up the risks of lining up a sniper shot, a chainsaw insta-kill, or making a desperate dash for cover. It's a turn-based tactics shooter with a missing pause button. There's a reason that it translated so smoothly to a tactics spin-off.
(Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) E-Day introduces new weaponry that makes cowering in cover harder than ever. It loves a blast of acid, this game, either delivered from a massive evil frog or a new gun that shotguns it at you. Devastating, but a loving kiss on the cheek compared to the Goreshot, a grappling hook only interested in grappling your torso from your body. So gloriously over-the-top, it almost makes up for the insta-kill tedium from the elite enemy who wields it.
That stuff's good, but it's the renovations to the old guard that stand out. The spike trap now opens with a hugely satisfying thunk-thunk-thunk as its horrible insides prepare themselves for a good gouging. The explosive arrow-firing torque bow gets a great glow up—the sound design as it finds its target is wonderful, practically a doomsday drum roll, so good I still enjoy it even when a locust is aiming it at me. And if I'm ever called upon to assassinate God, this game's sublime sniper rifle is what I'm reaching for.
So if the gunplay's a treat and the core combat never better, what's the problem? Well, almost everything else, unfortunately.
Dis-may
E-Day is a prequel, referring to the fateful day when the locust got bored of living underground and burst free from the surface to say a very messy hello. This is covered in the opening cutscene of the original Gears of War. And if you're wondering what insights E-Day has that weren't covered in said cutscene, same here.
The game opens with Marcus Fenix and Dom 'boy isn't it great that my wife and kids are alive' Santiago. Instead of the cynical, traumatised, seen-it-all-before combat veteran of the original Gears, here Marcus is… a cynical, traumatised, seen-it-all-before combat veteran. Oh.
(Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) Discovering Marcus was once a flamboyant drag queen who was changed forever by E-Day into the man we know today was probably too much to hope for. But the fact he's essentially exactly the frikkin' same is the first alarm bell that this prequel is struggling to justify its own existence.
Is the shooting strong enough to sustain this? Yeah, just, though it does get exhausting.
Once the locust arrive, E-Day tries cosplaying as Resident Evil for a bit, complete with a trip through the panicking city to the police station. Some of these horror moments work. The drone gets an excellent introduction, though not so much for the poor sap stuck in the interrogation room with it. Other attempts at horror atmosphere are hilariously clumsy. I find the blood-soaked helmet of a transit worker, and the game immediately shatters any sense of foreboding with text popping up saying 'Bloody Transit Worker's Helmet Found!' Er, hooray?
The game then has some dumb fun giving little origin stories to its iconography—chainsaws being attached to machine guns! Grenades being tossed in emergence holes! Problem is, by the start of Act 2, you have the weaponry, armor, and the squad. At which point E-Day just becomes standard Gears of War again. You explore the ruined city (not open-world, more wide-ish linear) with goals never more complicated than 'shoot those locusts' or 'survive this wave of locusts' or 'why haven't you shot those locusts yet?'
(Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) Gears 5 understood the value of variety. It had sections where you had to stealth around a mad scientist's factory to stealth kill infected robots. Or ride a skiff down an icy mountain. Or fight an enemy on the stage of a Hamilton-inspired musical which starts rotating at the worst moment possible (play Gears 5— it's one of the best 7/10s ever ).
True, not all of Gears 5's ideas worked. But I wanted a sequel that improved upon them, not a regression that believes the only thing you should ever be doing in one of these games is endlessly pulling the trigger. It's just slightly remixed combat encounters all the way down. Battle a giant frog and several snipers! OK, now two frogs, one sniper, and several shotgunners! OK, OK, now three giant spiders that fire insta-kill rockets, and loads of grunts, and the last checkpoint was seven minutes back! …Hey, why are you suddenly aiming at me?
Is the shooting strong enough to sustain this? Yeah, just, though it does get exhausting. It's an action movie with everything ripped out that isn't bullets going into bastards. The 20+ hour campaign is also waaaaay too long considering how one-note it is (well, aside from two crap shooting-from-a-turret-inside-a-helicopter bits, but I was planning on being nice and not bringing those up).
(Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) Moderate improvements
New for E-Day are mod slots for your weapons and armour. Mods include less recoil, better scopes, faster chainsaw revving, etc. Not as useless and incremental as the crap you get in [insert whichever live service shooter you currently have the most beef with here], but it's borderline and hard to get excited about. Far better is the gizmo that can send out rippling shockwaves that stun enemies, perfect for a chainsawin'. I found a mod for it that also sets enemies on fire. Lovely.
You get these mods for completing sidequests or finding them in cases. But E-Day is so terrified of you missing anything that tiresome all-caps text saying HARD CASE NEARBY blazes across the screen. And the location of the case is immediately added to your map. Oh and if you activate whatever this game's version of Eagle Vision is called, we'll show you exactly where the case is. Ugh.
Gears 5—which I promise to stop swooning over soon—did all this so much more elegantly. You had a robot companion with abilities that were upgraded with currency you found through exploring. No map markers, screaming text, or other BS that belongs in the Ubisoft dark ages. You were actually incentivised to explore properly, with any world-building or character moments you encountered along the way a nice bonus.
(Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) E-Day's a less interesting place to explore regardless. A city in ruin is one of gaming's most overdone settings, so you really have to pull out the stops to make it interesting, like in The Last of Us 2, or the opening Leon section of Resident Evil Requiem. Otherwise, seen one ruined city block, seen 'em all, like in the second half of Resident Evil Requiem (at least E-Day is less grey and brown, shockingly).
How can a game with such outstanding skull-popping, blood-geysering headshots still have such pitiful damage feedback against elite enemies?
Other frustrations just feel like they shouldn't be happening in the seventh game of a series. There's a special place in hell for games that put checkpoints before long dialogue exchanges that you can't skip through. Normal difficulty still isn't challenging enough. Opt for hardcore and you get the compelling challenge, but also have to swallow the occasional ocean of stale piss, with boss health bars so overlong I'm amazed they fit on the screen.
And how can a game with such outstanding skull-popping, blood-geysering headshots still have such pitiful damage feedback against elite enemies? There's no satisfaction in emptying clip after clip into a monster, not feeling like you're having any impact whatsoever until it finally falls over. Do I actually love E-Day's sniper rifle, or is it the only gunshot against the more bullet-spongy cretins that feels like it has any kick?
A new enemy at least has the decency to have a nice big eye that it doesn't like being shot in, which means I actually feel the impact of my gunfire. This thing is called… actually, to try and describe it myself when I can let the game do that in the following screenshot would be like snatching the pen from Shakespeare. My apologies. Take it away, E-Day:
(Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) Thank you, Lucas. God this game is infuriating. Great shooting trapped in a horribly overstretched campaign, telling a story that clearly didn't long to be told. It feels more like Microsoft taking a page out of the Jack Donaghy playbook and tapping a sign saying 'make it 2007 again'. Marcus is gonna have to open Gears 6 with one Hell of a drag show to make up for this.
Multiplayer saves the E-Day
Multiplayer is a less qualified success. The 4-v-4 modes are great if you just want to jump right in and quickly discover that you should have been practicing with the shotgun a lot more during the campaign. Conquest is all about taking and holding a certain section of the map, Demolition is all about triggering and protecting a bomb somewhere the opposing team would rather you didn't, and so on.
Horde Siege is a fun, smart evolution of what came before, an experience that tries to expand what Gears can be.
Nothing revolutionary, but all executed well, and even fun when you get matched against bots. I like how the new jump button means leaping over insta-death chasms is now an option. Which The Coalition have celebrated by sneaking in a bunch of insta-death chasms that are easy to miss, the cads.
Horde Siege is more ambitious as it takes advantage of the city's massive scope. Classic horde saw you setting up defenses like spike traps and turrets before waves of enemies came to tear them down. That's still true here, except now that Horde is basically open-world, there's a lot of commuting between the actual wave-battling bits. But where that padded out an irritatingly wheel-spinny campaign, it works here because the city feels much more alive and spontaneous.
(Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) Optional objectives with tasty rewards constantly pop-up, tempting you and your team to hunt down a massive enemy, or carry a core across the city that essentially leaves one of you unarmed. Even if you ignore these because you've unfortunately matched with the dullest squad alive, locusts can still suddenly appear in big numbers at any moment. Not so often that it becomes as exhausting as the campaign, but enough to give even a long encounter-free trudge across the city constant tension.
You're on a squad of four, and there are two other squads out there, too. Occasionally you might cross paths and can join them for a bit of shooting, or maybe they'll save you. There's not much incentive to do so—besides, y'know, compassion or whatever—but it's still a fun touch.
Horde Siege is a fun, smart evolution of what came before, and an experience that tries to expand what Gears can be. It'll still be worth playing whether The Coalition decides to build on it or not. I just wish it didn't feel like it was living in such a separate silo to a flawed solo adventure that's disappointingly conservative in comparison.

title: The PC Gamer Mysteries, Case #1, 'A Slice of Death': Why is there a dead golfer hidden in Golden Tee '99?
text:
"Golden Tee '99, hole seven, Aspen Lake: There's a dead body about 180 yards out, a little bit to the right in the woods there," says Keith of Keith's Arcade, a YouTube channel not typically devoted to cold case homicides. But as they say in golf, you've got to play it as it lies, and in November 2012 Keith stumbled upon a body lying motionless just off the green of the otherwise picturesque, forested course in northern Colorado. It was his responsibility to tell the world what he'd found.
"There you go. There you go," Keith repeats, clearly in shock. "Dead body in the woods, about 180 yards from the tee off point. Hole seven, Aspen Lake, Golden Tee '99. Thanks for watching."
That's a dead body, all right. You can tell because of the pixels. (Image credit: Incredible Technologies) Under the pixelated body is a pool of blood, suggesting this unidentified man lying facedown in the grass met a violent end. A golf club stretches out from his hand—but was he really a golfer? Or was it placed there to make it look like a tragic accident, an injury sustained during what is well-known to be a dangerous game? Were there clouds suddenly darkening over the course beside Aspen Lake, or were those just scanlines?
Golfers, famously, take their lives into their own hands every time they get in one of those little carts (no seatbelts!!) and drive it, like, 200 yards. Perhaps that's why this death went uninvestigated for so long—it's even conspicuously absent from the Colorado Bureau of Investigation's cold case files, at least according to my comprehensive independent examination (typing the word "golf" into the database, getting zero results and immediately giving up).
To solve a case this cold, I knew there was only one place to go: straight to the source.
Bogey in the rough
Just one problem. Like any other professional true crime investigator (better known as a "podcaster"), I stumbled upon this case with little clue of who to get in touch with first and a keen awareness of the fact that even if I did, jumping right to the solution would ruin all the suspense. So I started by getting the email of a friend-of-a-friend, whose earliest credit on Mobygames happened to be Golden Tee '99.
"I vaguely remember that this was a thing, but unfortunately I don't know how it got in," artist Stephen Alexander—who went on to work on BioShock and BioShock Infinite—told me last year. "If I had to guess it would have been put there by Jim Zielinski (the course designer). He did pretty much all art placements in that version of the game since it was almost all gameplay relevant. Outside of that I really don't know. I was credited on '99, but I think I just did the logo animation (if even that)? I had started pretty recently and was working on some other 3D stuff that was being started up at the time."
A promising lead! Armed with a suspect, I did what any aspiring podcaster would do in this situation: Sit on the information for a month, then track down what might be Jim Zielinski's email, fire off a single message at 5:52 pm, and then completely drop the story as soon as no response was forthcoming.
The third caddie
(Image credit: Getty Images - Luis Moreno / 500px) Everyone in the professional investigating-fake-dead-bodies-in-30-year-old-golf-games sphere has something that drives them. A tragedy in their past. An unwavering, ironclad sense of justice. A Turfman 800.
For me, it's procrastination. Faced with some other task I really didn't want to do in March 2026, I reopened the case and found another lead. Software engineer Tino Kalafatis has little online presence, but with a bit of searching I uncovered that he has, like Zielinski, worked at Golden Tee creator Incredible Technologies since the 1980s . This time my email found its target.
An ace gumshoe himself, Tino did what had previously proven slightly difficult for this reporter: he asked Jim.
(Image credit: HBO, John Oliver) …who, I should be very clear, did not in fact murder a man on a Colorado golf course . But he did cheekily place a little pixelated body on hole seven of Aspen Lake in Golden Tee '99, as a goof.
"Yes this is legit. Back in the day we thought it would be fun to put some interesting things to look at off in the woods in case players made an errant shot. The dead guy was my idea, and it's actually a digitized photo of me laying in the grass outside our office. We digitized the photo and put it into the game," said the man himself, as relayed over email by Kalafatis.
Turns out this was never a fake murder investigation at all. It was a fake suicide investigation all along.
As he's described on the Incredible Technologies golf-focused blog LiveWire , Zielinski is "a guy who loves golf, who strives to create golf games for other people who love golf, and he’s damn good at it." Before co-creating Golden Tee, he was the arcade company's "first and only QA employee," before bonding with programmer Larry Hogdson over "their shared love of the gentlemen's game" and taking on course design for a fledgling golf simulator. That project didn't pan out, but it eventually led to the creation of Golden Tee. They've been making golf games ever since.
You may still be reeling from the twist that Golden Tee's course mastermind once put a photograph of his own "dead" body in the woods of hole seven of Aspen Lake in Golden Tee '99. But it turns out this wasn't an isolated incident. Bodies have also been spotted in Golden Tee 2010 and whichever one this is . The sport remains dangerous, no matter how much more sophisticated golf game technology grows with each passing year.
Cover-up!?!?
(Image credit: Digital Eclipse, Incredible Technologies) Last year, after stumbling across Keith of Keith's Arcade's video about the dead body in the woods, about 180 yards from the tee off point on hole seven of Aspen Lake in Golden Tee '99, I went looking for it myself in the recently released Golden Tee Arcade Classics collection on Steam.
There I made a chilling discovery: The body, which we now know was the digitized flesh of Jim Zielinski, placed by the physical flesh of Jim Zielinski, was right where it should be… but the blood wasn't .
Was this a flaw in the emulation used to present these arcade games on PC? Or an attempt to make golf look less cutthroat? Who took the blood, and what did they do with it?
These hard-hitting questions, put to compilation developer Digital Eclipse, have so far gone unanswered. Complicating the situation, if you play Golden Tee '99 on the Internet Archive —where it runs in arcade emulator MAME—the pool of blood is there. So what's different about the Arcade Classics version? Even Zielinski isn't sure, though he offered his own theory.
The dead body in Golden Tee '99 in MAME. Note the blood. Incredible Technologies The dead body in Golden Tee '99 in the Digital Eclipse collection. No blood. Incredible Technologies, Digital Eclipse "There may have been two versions, the original one with blood, and then one where we got rid of the blood puddle," he said. "For a lot of the early Golden Tee 3D golf courses, I also placed a digitized version of myself directly behind the first tee, so my friends and family could easily find me in the game. They just had to start a game, turn around 180 degrees, and I'd be standing there."
I asked if the original photo used to add Jim to the game was still around somewhere, but he said it's sadly been lost to time. By cross-referencing the Arcade Database , however, I was able to determine that Incredible Technologies did release two revisions of Golden Tee '99: v1.00 and v1.00S. S for… hole seven ? S for sanitized ? S for sans blood ?
(Image credit: Incredible Technologies) Bound by my duty, I found a ROM of Golden Tee '99 v1.00S online and loaded it into MAME. I started noticing more stuff on each course that I swear wasn't there before. There were more spectators, more not-so-hidden bits of eye candy that oozed Zielinskism. A woman in a polka dot bathing suit sunbathing behind a log cabin. A guy on a lawnmower. A cheery group in a bright yellow raft paddling alongside the fairway. I hadn't seen these versions of the Aspen Lake front nine before. And when I got to hole seven, about 180 yards out, a little bit to the right in the woods, there was Jim, sure enough. And there was Jim's blood.
Toss that theory into the sand trap, then.
Perhaps that S actually stood for something a little more sinister—something Digital Eclipse was simply trying to distract me from with that missing blood. Keep me focused on the body, not on what else was going on around the course. But it didn't work, because on my way to hole seven I found something to blow this whole case wide open. Something lurking in the woods, just behind the green. Something that suspiciously disappeared when I tried to get too close.
S… FOR SASQUATCH!?!?
(Image credit: Incredible Technologies) I've taken this investigation as far as it can go. Time to bring in the experts .

title: 'Please give Novus one more chance': An 11-year-old early access survival game just got its first update since 2018
text:
What happened?
Early access survival game Novus Inceptio got a major update this week
It's the game's first update since 2018
The game entered early access in October 2015 (and is still in early access)
The solo dev says "the energy and the will to finish the project are back"
The map has gone from 9 km² to 64 km² of "pure wilderness"
Combat has been rebuilt
It's now singleplayer but there are plans for co-op
Responses have been edited for length and clarity.
PC Gamer: Why did development stop for so long?
Martin Markus Mastný: I jumped into Unity head first, learned C# and learned how to work with Unity. That went on from 2013 until the early access release on October 5, 2015: learning, making the game, trying things. The whole time I had this strong idea and excitement that one day it would be an MMORPG. I built the server layer and databases and connected it all to Unity.
Then Steam slapped me in the face :) Suddenly I had to deal with a million other things: PR, sales, the community, bugs, people's reactions.
When I opened the Steam forum in the morning and questions were still unanswered, I had to answer them myself right away. So my community manager ended up handling bugs and being my quiet advisor. I needed to react immediately so people got a response. I felt I had to accommodate everyone and thank them for playing the game.
The result was total collapse and burnout. It basically ruined the whole game, too.
Martin Markus Mastný
My day looked like this: get up, deal with the community, work on the game all day and deal with the community while doing it. No time off at all. I went full time like that from early 2016 until 2019, nonstop. And I kept making compromises to please people, to get good reviews, to give everyone what they asked for. The result was total collapse and burnout. It basically ruined the whole game, too. It turned into something it was never supposed to be. Now, years later, I can see it in the code and in the mechanics, and I'm trying to bring it all back and fix it.
Why return to Novus Inceptio now?
(Image credit: McMagic Productions) It's about fulfilling a dream. I had that dream and that vision, and I know I can't fulfill it 100%, that's not realistic. But whenever I launched the game, the world and the environment gave me a really nice feeling. I could spend an hour just running through the forest, enjoying the landscape and listening to music. That's why I went back to it.
It's a kind of responsibility to all those people, to close this chapter fairly and well. This game is a big chapter of my life, and it changed my life for better and for worse. I have that commitment and I want to keep it: finish the game to a state where I'm happy with it.
Some inner tension and emotion when I talk about the game, I don't even know exactly what it is. It's like my child. When someone curses at it, it's hard for me, because I put it together as well as I could.
What's your message to skeptical players?
I can't promise anything and I don't want to.
Martin Markus Mastný
That's a hard one. The way I see it now, the roughly seven-year break didn't happen. I had to erase it in my head and tell myself I'm back in 2019 and moving on, just with new experience from other projects.
I can't promise anything and I don't want to. The only thing I can say is: be patient and watch whether I keep going the way I'd like to. Early access gives me the chance to still change things while it's possible and to react to the community, which is what I've been doing the whole time anyway. So watch it if you want, and you'll see whether you give me that trust back or not.
Any advice for solo devs making survival games?
Make what you enjoy. Study other games and learn from their successes and their mistakes. But I wouldn't want to be in your shoes right now. It was hard in 2015 and today it's much harder. Look for new challenges, there's still a lot you can do in survival games.
I avoided classic co-op, and commercially it hurt the game a lot that it wasn't multiplayer. Sometimes you have to step back from your own vision when it's the thing dragging the game down. You can't see that at the time, only with distance, or when someone tells you from their own experience. I have that experience now, back then I didn't. Maybe that's the main advice.

title: My most-played album of 2026? Sorry, Mitski—it's Final Fantasy 10: House Grooves, a real thing that exists
text:
Final Fantasy music is presumably so profitable for Square Enix that there are always new ways to slice the pie, whether we're talking piano covers, guitar versions, or expensive anniversary vinyl releases of its classic RPG soundtracks.
Final Fantasy 10 is getting one of the latter next month to mark its 25th anniversary. And as someone who once spent a lot of my meagre convenience store salary importing the CD collection from Play Asia back in the day, it's undeniably a gorgeous sight:
(Image credit: Square Enix Music) Elsewhere, Square Enix continues to find more inventive ways to squeeze dollars out of its vast music catalogue, including some which push the music into different genres entirely. Final Fantasy 10: House Grooves —the second of its kind following a similar outing for FF9—is exactly what it sounds like. Can Final Fantasy 10's often mournful or moody score become dance music ?
The answer is: kind of. You never quite shake the sense that an unholy Seymour-Guado-and- his-mother -style union has taken place with this album.
Some of the remixes sound like music I'd expect to hear in the bar of the W hotel during GDC circa 2014. I'd say that definitely applies to the rendition of ' To Zanarkand ', the famous piano opening to the game. I get big 'making small talk with the concierge' energy from that one. Still, I do think the two styles ultimately gel in that case, even if the end result evokes vastly different feelings as piece of music.
' Phantoms ', a track players may remember from the icy Macalania sections of the game, is my favourite remix on there. I'd already heard this atmospheric track sampled in vapourwave and chillwave playlists from the mid-'10s, so the fit made sense there.
Then there are other times where the two styles don't totally mesh. Take ' Wandering ', perhaps the saddest track in the game, which plays after the evil cosmic whale Sin turns up early in the game and murders loads of soldiers on a beach. You can't really turn that one into a 'bop'—so it just ends up sounding like two totally separate pieces of music playing over the top of each other. I still enjoy listening to it, however, because my taste in music is dogshit.
The reason I suspect the entire album exists is to turn the game's most dancefloor-friendly boss theme into a legit club banger. Give it up for ' Fight with Seymour ', which also slaps the Blitzball theme hook in there for good measure. Still, I wouldn't play this at a party, unless only my most accepting dweeb friends were the ones on the guest list.
No one's going to be spinning Final Fantasy 10: House Grooves on Boiler Room any time soon, but considering it's reheated nostalgia, I am very satisfied. It's an unhealthy level of pandering by Square Enix to the FF10 sickos like me, yet here I am, ready to play these house 'grooves' for the 20th time.

title: PSA: Star Wars Galactic Racer pilots, put some points in resilience before you hit the acid planet
text:
The multiplayer tour mode in Galactic Racer lets you upgrade a speeder over the course of six races while other players manically shunt you into the wall on every track. It's a best-of-both-worlds mode that adds a little of the campaign's run-based progression to a multiplayer tournament.
But since you only get one race on each planet, you might be blindsided by Sentinel I. Locations in Galactic Racer tend to follow the Star Wars pattern of single-environment worlds—the desert planet, the jungle planet—and good old Sentinel I is apparently the galaxy's planet of burning piss.
Veer a little off-track on Sentinel I and you'll hit boiling yellow acid that quickly tanks your ramjet boost. It's a bad time. While it's normally tempting to throw your precious upgrade points into afterburner and ramjet to get your speed as high as possible, and battery if you've got a decent ability you need more energy for, make sure to put some points in resilience before you get to Sentinel 1 so you aren't instantly tanked the screwed you skim over one of its scenic acid rivers.
It'll come in handy later on as well, because the climactic race of each tour on Derven Acos is basically a remix of previous environments and their hazards—including a little bit of Ando Prime's freezing ice, Lantaana's lava, and Sentinel I's corrosive acid. The same tip applies in singleplayer, of course, but there you'll start with a bunch of tuning points earned in previous runs and be less starved for upgrades.

title: 2026 is a low-key revolutionary year for player movement in games
text:
A lot of the 3D games I consider touchstones of thoughtful player movement are a decade or more old: Mirror's Edge, of course, Titanfall 2, Dishonored 2, Doom Eternal or ARMA 3. That's by no means a comprehensive list, but these are the games that come to mind when I think about in-game movement that feels incredibly considered. And if ARMA 3 feels out of place in that list, its sim-style tactical physicality is memorable to anyone who plays it even briefly (me).
These each set the ceiling high for what you could achieve with their controls, if you were prepared to learn them. Each offered a power fantasy of some kind to be mastered, whether you're wall-running onto a mech or peeking out across a field to line up a perfect shot.
In recent years, though, I feel like it's increasingly common to find developers who want to capture granular, basic movements from real life that have no power fantasy element whatsoever. Things that would've sounded so boring if they were back-of-the-box features during the age of Quake 2 and Half-Life. I'm talking about walking slowly. Steadily moving up a cliff face. Mantling awkwardly over surfaces. Getting defeated by a slightly high rock and taking the long way around. Falling on your arse if you tumble down a small hill.
They're about finding the fun in something as simple as balancing the packages you're carrying in Death Stranding, or escaping the mud in Snowrunner. 'Boring' games with a simulation aspect are as old as PC gaming itself, but this newer crop are tapping into something more universal and compelling that strikes a chord with players. Some of these games have ended up being GOTY frontrunners.
It was 2025's Baby Steps that got me thinking about this in more detail. The idea that just the act of walking without falling over into physics hell could be the entire game was maybe not revolutionary by itself, but the high-end execution was an important distinction. There's something about Baby Steps that I find uniquely pure: it breaks down a fundamental and often just functional part of any other game—putting one foot in front of another, then slowly repeating it—into its constituent parts, then rebuilds it. Every step matters. Every part of every step.
It's a beloved and award-winning game. I didn't finish it, but did throw two expletive-filled afternoons at it, and I respect the heck out of what it tries to accomplish.
The irony is, even though Baby Steps is not a power fantasy by most people's criteria, it was inspired by a game that clearly is one. Well, inspired by a particularly gruelling custom map for it, anyway: The Mirror's Edge mod Stratocubulus got you to rethink everything about Faith's moveset in the game and experiment with the level geometry in order to solve it. "It was the stuff that was ambiguous as to whether or not you could do it, stuff that you could puzzle over and push you into trying new ways of moving," said designer Gabe Cuzillo at GDC 2026, as captured by Wes . "That was really the experience we're interested in."
Some of this year's best games are distinguished because of how they use movement, too. There's Cairn, which turns climbing a mountain into a series of precise navigation puzzles with a resource management layer. There's Control Resonant, which marries a familiar superhero-style moveset to brain-bending switches in gravity. There's Vholume , which initially seems like a more stripped back version of Mirror's Edge parkour, except it's hiding incredible depth in its level layouts and mechanics.
Doom: The Dark Ages' Revelations DLC added the chain spear, giving it some of Eternal's arena acrobatics, while Cicadamata 's queasy FOV manipulation and towering triple jumps make it a singular proposition as a game about navigating a combat arena.
(Image credit: flowergarden) Then, of course, you have Big Walk, which is an entire game of trotting across a large map from A to B. The fantasy element is taking that journey with friends, but the actual walking part is not that easy. Just mantling over a knee-high surface can be challenging.
I don't think these games are deliberately part of a trend, but I do have a couple of theories on why we're seeing so much experimentation with movement. One is that this is the natural outcome of how long 3D games have been around now. There truly is a game for everything these days, whether it's a man walking around in a babygrow or the nightmare fuel sitting in the bottom rungs of Steam.
My second theory is that it's a reaction to control being taken from players with the rise of big-budget blockbusters in the late 2000s and 2010s. These things ebb and flow: Much like how action games have been curving towards hardcore combat inspired by FromSoftware games, players (and designers) are now drawn to a similar level of stimulation and craft in their character movement, whether they're about boring old walking or turning the player into Spider-Man.
Stripped back
Years ago I listened to an episode of Irrational Games' podcast where one of the developers pointed out that a reason Grand Theft Auto 3 was revolutionary was that it condensed what could've been a complex sequence of actions into a single button press: opening the door to a car, removing the driver, climbing into the car, turning the key and taking the steering wheel. GTA turned that into "Triangle." I don't know if I agreed with that theory—GTA 1 did it first in 1997—but I can see why a designer might think about it that way.
In general, the rise of big-budget multiplatform games started pushing PC games more towards console norms in terms of interface and how they played, in the name of offering an identical experience across all platforms. For movement, this marked a trend towards third-person games like Assassin's Creed, a series where very little input is needed to make your character climb across a series of rooftops.
That influence still extends to games like Ghost of Tsushima or Wolverine, where movement is trivial because you're only allowed to interact with certain parts of the game world. A jump doesn't exactly feel like a jump. Likewise, Uncharted—a series I love—sanded all the sharp edges off Tomb Raider's '90s platforming. Friction was stripped back in order to get millions of people to play. It worked.
(Image credit: Game Bakers) I personally feel that type of design is falling out of fashion. The reason games like Cairn, Baby Steps or Big Walk connect now is that they don't trivialise movement in this way. This is why I think these games could only exist now, with a very long history of 3D movement behind us.
There's something subversive about designers taking a step back and asking, 'well, what is movement, actually?' What do you have to accomplish to put one foot in front of the other? What happens to your body's positioning when you place the weight behind your left arm against a cliff face? Those are more interesting questions to ask than I ever thought they could be. There may be a whole universe of games inside those limitations.
Next up: let's take another step back and get even more granular about human movement. How about an incredibly hardcore 15-hour game just about the act of breathing, culminating with the objective to tie your shoelaces while holding in a gut? I'd find these motions even more relatable than Nate's trials in Baby Steps. I can see the GOTY nominations already.

title: Quarterfinals: Vote for the best RTS unit of all time
text:
Friends, we are doing important work—the work of determining, through democracy and science (maybe), what RTS unit deserves to be held aloft and named the greatest RTS unit of all time. It's a lot of responsibility.
Last week, the war began. 16 units entered, 8 units survived . There were close battles. Dawn of War's unstable Psyker and Battle for Middle-earth's Rohirrim were neck and neck for most of the voting period, swapping positions with every blow traded. But in the end, those long-haired horse boys won. Then there were the ass-kickings. Right from the word go, Warcraft's Peon raked in the votes, leaving Rise of Legends' majestic Glass Dragon battered a bruised.
We salute the losers—they were good, but not good enough. And now the victors must return to the battlefield to duke it out again. It's time for the quarterfinals, baby!
The quarterfinals bracket
(Image credit: BracketHQ) Things are getting tense. We're going to have to make some difficult decisions. Will our collective love for funny little green guys keep the Peon from being obliterated by the mighty Mammoth Tank? Will the Mirage Tank's ability to pretend to be a tree help it survive against Darth Vader's personal Star Destroyer? This is all up to you.
All four of my personal picks made it to the quarterfinals (thank you, thank you), but now I'm nervous. Now that we're down to eight competitors, I've got a pick in each fight. I could win it all! Or I could lose everything. Harrowing stuff. I'm particularly worried about the Dolphin vs Priest battle. Our sleek, squeaky pal utterly dominated the Sonic Tank in the last round, but the Priest was incredibly popular—only the Peon had a more clear-cut battle.
It would be inappropriate for me to try and influence your vote, but just let me ask you this: do you really want to see a heroic, noble creature of the sea getting crushed by organised religion? Let your conscience guide you.
As before, you'll be able to vote on each battle below until the end of Sunday (BST) . Otherwise, there are no rules. Chaos reigns! Vote based on vibes, aesthetic, hyper-specific grudges or just who you think would win in a fight. Right, let's get back to the war!
Peon vs Mammoth Tank
Peon (Warcraft 3)
(Image credit: Blizzard) The real heroes of Warcraft, Peons are mistreated, disrespected and undervalued by orcish society, but they are the most critical cog in the Horde's war machine. They get called "dogs" and "cowards", and yeah, they might enjoy the occasional nap—but they work hard! They deserve a rest!
Orcs are classist dickheads. Without Peons, you'd have no great halls, no barracks, no trained warriors. Peons avoid conflict not because they are cowards, but because they know they are too important to die in battle—that the future of their people hinges on them building a new gold mine or chopping down some trees.
And if it comes down to it, they'll fight, either directly (which they are, frankly, terrible at) or by holing up in a burrow. They can do it all! Zug zug, my friends. Zug zug. —Fraser Brown, Online Editor
Mammoth Tank
(Image credit: EA) God bless these great, trundling beasts—implacable Soviet strength wrought in steel and pig iron.
Mammoth Tanks are unfathomably costly and painfully slow, but whatever . I'm convinced just one of them could probably win the entire RA1 Soviet campaign by itself. Akh-knowledged. —Joshua Wolens, News Writer
Rohirrim vs Pride of Hiigara
Rohirrim (Lord of the Rings: Battle for Middle-earth)
(Image credit: EA) The Ride of the Rohirrim is a very influential movie moment for a young lad. I, for example, decided that the only faction I could play in Lord of the Rings: Battle for Middle-earth was Rohan. And the only unit I would enjoy playing were the Rohirrim.
I'd get my long-haired horse boys fresh out of the stable, hand them forged blades (made the tips of their spears glow), as much heavy armour as I could afford, then arrange them into a neatly-formed flying V formation. My entire operation was focused on powering through as fast as possible until I could get my horde of superpowered spearmen on horseback. Every playthrough—every damn playthrough.
These Rohirrim were basically a cheat code. They could easily trample Sauron's armies under hoof. Just line them up, set them off, and watch carnage ensue. I'm rewatching the Ride of the Rohirrim as I write this and it makes me want to boot the game right back up again—goosebumps. —Jacob Ridley, Managing Editor, Hardware
Pride of Hiigara (Homeworld 2)
(Image credit: Gearbox) While other ships are spitting out missiles and other little projectiles, the Homeworld Mothership is spitting out capital ships. It is both a unit and your base—an impossibly huge mobile factory that can carry your whole fleet inside of it. Its direct offensive capabilities are extremely limited, but like I said: It can spit out capital ships.
I've picked the Kushan/Hiigaran version specifically because of its iconic design, which for me is right up there with the Enterprise D and Star Destroyers. While it's largely stationary in the original Homeworld (at least in the campaign), it's fully mobile in Homeworld 2, giving it an extra dose of utility. —Fraser Brown, Online Editor
Mirage Tank vs Super Star Destroyer
Mirage Tank (Command and Conquer: Red Alert 3)
(Image credit: EA) Most tanks are performative. They're like those folks who film themselves in the gym, flexing their muscles, grunting and getting in everyone's way. But not the Mirage Tank—it's sneaky. You wouldn't even notice it in the gym. You'd just be left to wonder, "Who put this tree in the gym?" And then it cuts right through you with its spectrum dispersion cannon.
It was already one of the coolest units ever created in Red Alert 2, but Red Alert 3's version introduces more disguises and enhances the unit's DPS capabilities. It can be a sneaky assassin on its own, but a group of them can make short work of an enemy base. —Fraser Brown, Online Editor
Executor Super Star Destroyer (Star Wars: Empire at War)
(Image credit: Lucasfilm) My colleagues have, for some reason, chosen to prioritize things like "funny voice lines" and "subtext" while proposing their favorite RTS units. Sorry, gang: you're about to get crushed by 19 kilometers of steel and turbolasers.
This enormous Death Triangle is the ultimate wish fulfilment vessel in Empire at War, one of my favorite Star Wars games. It's not a top-tier RTS, but it is top-tier Star Wars fantasy in game form, letting you move around a bunch of little toy ships and play out the "what if" of throwing Rogue Squadron's ace pilots up against a Star Destroyer. They've got a real chance in that fight, but not against the Executor, Darth Vader's personal ride.
The damn thing is practically the size of Manhattan, and you can really feel that scale in the game. It makes regular Star Destroys look like Doritos by comparison. It's swimming with so many turbolaser batteries it can bully an entire Rebel fleet by itself. Don't even try that A-Wing trick against it—that sort of nonsense only works in the movies. —Wes Fenlon, Senior Editor
Dolphin vs Priest
Dolphin (Command and Conquer: Red Alert 2)
(Image credit: EA) The Dolphin—what a superstar. You could be forgiven for treating these sleek, squeaky critters like nothing more than scouts, with their lack of armour and impressive speed. But you'd be wrong. They are killers.
In a group, Dolphins are unstoppable gods of war, able to deftly take out buildings and vessels with their sonic blasts. They should be feared and respected. Sure, the Soviets think they have naval superiority, but once the Allies start churning out Dolphins, it's game over, man. —Fraser Brown, Online Editor
Priest (Age of Empires)
(Image credit: Xbox) "Wololo." I win. —Jody Macgregor, Weekend Editor

title: Critical Role's latest D&D episode was so stressful, I discovered a new noise my mouth can make
text:
Last week, I said that I wasn't entirely sure who would make it out of Critical Role's next episode . Well, the next episode has happened, and let me tell you—I was absolutely, concretely right in that assumption. Spoilers for Critical Role episode 37, if you've not watched it yet.
The episode opened with the attempted assassination of one Wicander Halovar. Two hours later, they had successfully completed the first round. This isn't because anyone at the table is bad at playing D&D, it's because there were a ton of moving parts:
A Hold Person spell, two assassins with three attacks each, a Command spell from Wic's father to force him to accept his fate, guards who weren't in on the scheme rushing in to protect him, his mother desperately trying to stop it all from happening, his little brother being held back, Tyranny sprinting down the streets of Dol-Makjar to get to the theatre, everyone else barrelling through the stands: Utter chaos.
It's an incredibly difficult thing to do, stacking the deck so thoroughly against one player. On the one hand, you want to do justice to the world everyone's playing in—Wicander messed it up with his wannabe religious dictator grandma, so she decided to have him bumped off. But on the other hand, Wic simply getting instagibbed wouldn't make for a good game.
Even still, the deck was toppling high. Hold Person grants auto-crits to melee attacks and requires a Wisdom saving throw, and Wic has a whopping zero for an ability modifier. What's more, the person casting it clung tight onto concentration, and was vanishing into the crowd. And god, was it close. On his final death save, a bardic inspiration that was a mere one short on the die spelled the end for Wicander Halovar.
Here's where some consternation from the more diehard rules lawyers of the fanbase comes in—particularly those who want the game to be more brutal: Brennan, seeing this unfold, decided to give Sam Riegel a devil's bargain. Make one last save with disadvantage, or release Tyranny from her bondage to his evil family.
If he made the save—which is a roughly 30% chance at disadvantage, since he needed both dice to be a 10 or higher—he'd be able to hold onto his life. If he didn't make that save? He'd die anyway, and Tyranny would be doomed. Or he could go quietly into that good night and release Tyranny for his sacrifice. For some, this scans as going easy, to which I say: Phooey. A few things!
A 70% chance of the absolute worst-case scenario cannot, in a sane mind, be considered "going easy" on someone.
Riegel was, understandably (everyone was stressed) under a lot of pressure to go against his first instinct, which was to just pop the shield spell. Which would've saved him from the attack that put him a single save away from death to begin with.
It kinda sucks to spend a multi-hour combat just making saving throws while fearing for your character's life.
Anyway, In a moment that will live forever in my memory, Riegel took a moment to look at his dice tray while his panicking, stress-ulcer suffering table flurried around him to look for a way to help, and dropped two dice into the tray. A 12 and a 13: A success.
When this happened, I made a noise.
I can't quite put the noise into words—I wish I had recorded it—but it was not a noise I had made before. It was something between a laugh and a yell. I sort of went "HAAA!" The emphasis on the H was gummy and flimsy, like my primal ape brain, buried in my amygdala, was trying to reach down my stem and out of my throat to throw a rock at my screen. I am considering calling this noise a portmanteau of laugh and yell. A lell. A laull? I'm working on it.
In case you've not started watching Critical Role so far—and are one of those spoiler-immune people, in which case, bless you—let me tell you: This campaign is worth watching, it is absolutely some of the best actual play out there right now, and it will likely produce similarly novel noises from your mouth hole, as well.

title: I had 3 hours with Arc Raiders Frozen Trails update and spent most of it playing with the new grapple hook
text:
The grapple hook is a legit game changer
Yeeeeeeeeehooooooooooo!
Yeah yeah, sure, Arc Raiders is getting some new guns, but the real star of my session was the grapple hook. Embark made an honest-to-god grapple hook: Not the kind that zips you straight to where you aim it (that already exists), but a simulated rope that's quite rare in videogames.
The grapple hook is only a green tier gadget, but very versatile. A single hook lets you:
Climb straight up to the top of most buildings
Swing from rooftop to rooftop like Spider-Man
Safely descend from tall buildings
Annoy the crap out of flying Arc bots
What makes the grapple hook so useful is that it sticks to just about anything . Wherever the hook lands becomes a pivot point that you can either climb toward, descend, or swing against. You can also redeploy the hook midair, without a cooldown or use limit, meaning you can chain swings together.
Above: Scaling a building with the grapple hook is about as fast as climbing a ladder, which is surprising.
It's a level of pendulum-based freedom that videogames rarely afford—let alone in a multiplayer environment—and makes the hook immediately fun to play with. The first match I had one, I ended up ignoring most of Pendola Pass' new locations and instead tried to see how long I could stay in the air with just the hook. I broke my ankles more than once, but in a short time I felt like the hook had tripled my movement options in Arc Raiders, and that's exciting. I really want to see how it performs on the other maps. Frozen Trail also adds a launcher that tethers two objects together and a grenade that yanks Arc bots to the ground, but I didn't test those thoroughly.
I'm delighted by Arc Raiders' embracing of physics-based tools and impressed that Embark isn't afraid to let these emergent gameplay ingredients be a little jank. You can tell while using the grapple hook why other videogames are so restrictive with similar mechanics: Sometimes you'll climb all the way up the rope only to not grab the ledge at the top, or the rope itself gets tangled between a protruding balcony, or you slide off the giant Emperor bot in Pendola Pass that Embark clearly doesn't want you to climb. It takes trial and error to use it well, and it's way more interesting than it is frustrating.
The skill tree rework is big… on paper
Arc Raiders' reworked skill tree is a mix of old and new abilities, with certain branches on the tree forcing you to pick one ability over others. Such as:
Is it just me, or is everyone gonna pick Mule's Gallop here? (Image credit: Embark Studios) Conditioning 10
Vault Spring: Lets you jump at the end of a vault
OR
Vaults On Vaults On Vaults: Vaulting no longer costs stamina.
Mobility 30
Sprinting on Fumes: Stamina never fully drains while sprinting.
OR
Wall Run: Sprinting at a wall allows you to run up it for a few steps.
OR
In The Flow: Chaining together mobility moves while sprinting increases the speed, and reduces the stamina cost.
(Image credit: Embark Studios) We were given a pile of XP points to dump into the skill tree. I focused on Mobility and Conditioning, and while it was nice to sprint for a long time without stopping, I can't say the new abilities led to me playing Arc Raiders any differently than before. The majority of the nodes on the tree are still incremental stat boosts that make the basics easier. It's a meaningful progression track in the long-term, but not instantly transformative so far.
To be fair, that may be exactly how it should be. Loot and crafting is the focus of Arc Raiders, and if the skill tree offered dramatic upgrades that make you a bigger threat, like better shields, it'd undermine other systems like the research tables and blueprints. This is an improvement, but I'm not clamoring for any one skill.
Pendola Pass is beautiful, but familiar
(Image credit: Embark Studios) I've played 80 hours of Marathon since the last time I booted Arc Raiders, and that game's tremendous maps left an impression on me. Each one not only looks and feels different, but has unique, gameplay-specific hooks that makes my destination a huge decision from the jump. Arc Raiders does this in smaller ways, but I've yet to discover the big hook of Pendola Pass.
If it's snow, then sure: The white blanket is visually unique, flash freezes are sort of a threat (though I didn't even encounter one by accident) and raiders appear to leave trails one could follow.
(Image credit: Embark Studios) If it's the new Bully Arc enemy, it's certainly an annoying new threat, though I plan to stay out of its way 90% of the time like I do the Leaper. When it comes to the stuff I do most in this game—plundering research facilities, stores, and residential districts—Pendola Pass feels like retreading chunks of existing maps.
Pendola Pass is welcome variety, but so far, it makes me wish Embark would take more Stella Montis-sized chances with its maps. Perhaps the real draw is getting inside the Emperor itself—I didn't manage it during the preview period, but it's apparently possible.

Anthropic 发布 Claude Haiku 5.5，运行成本平均降低约 75%

Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5

AI 导读

Anthropic 发布 Claude Haiku 5.5，定位为迄今最便宜、最快的小模型，适合摘要、压缩、数据库查询、分类等高吞吐任务，并可搭配 Opus 5.5 和 Sonnet 5.5 担任编码子智能体。

另有 13 家信源报道
正文 · AI 翻译
中文
原文

隆重推出 Claude Haiku 5.5：我们迄今为止发布的最便宜、最快、能力最强的小型模型。

Claude Haiku 5.5 专为高并发、成本敏感型任务而设计。它能可靠地处理快速且重复性的工作负载（如摘要、压缩、数据库查询和分类请求）。作为编码工作中的子代理，它与 Opus 5.5 和 Sonnet 5.5 搭配使用效果出色。而且，由于它也是我们迄今为止最快的模型，它尤其适合对速度敏感的任务，如实时客户支持和浏览器使用。¹

Haiku 5.5 的价格远低于 Haiku 4.5。平均而言，其运行成本现在降低了约 75%。²

伴随此次发布，我们也在提升整个模型系列的价值。我们将 Claude Sonnet 5.5 的缓存读取价格减半，这意味着 Sonnet 5.5 在大多数代理型工作上的运行成本现在降低了约 20%。此外，我们还为 Claude Max 和 Team 订阅用户推出了一项新的月度 API 额度，旨在支持用户在 Claude 平台上构建新的代理和应用程序。

性能

以下是 Claude Haiku 5.5 在一系列基准测试中的表现：

	Haiku 5.5	Haiku 4.5	GPT-6 Luna	Sonnet 5.5供参考
知识工作GDPval-AA v2.1	1620	735	1437	1840
知识工作AA-Briefcase v1.1	1578	614	1336	1824
计算机使用OSWorld 2.1	72.4%离线子集	15.7%离线子集	48.9%离线子集	83.9%离线子集
多学科推理Humanity’s Last Exam	45.9%无工具	10.2%无工具	—	56.9%无工具
57.4%使用工具	18.7%使用工具	—	64.5%使用工具
代理型编码Terminal-Bench 4.0	39.2%	0.0%	16.4%	70.6%
代理型编码FrontierCode 1.1 (Main)	46.4%	—	42.4%	52.1%Xhigh
视觉推理Chartography	46.4%无工具	6.4%无工具	29.1%无工具	61.6%无工具

有关我们如何运行评估的详细信息，请参阅 Haiku 5.5 系统卡。

Haiku 5.5 是我们首个配备可调节努力程度设置的 Haiku 级模型。这意味着，与我们的其他模型一样，用户可以选择是优化成本还是优化智能。下图展示了 Haiku 5.5 在每个努力程度设置下在三项基准测试中的表现：

OSWorld 2.1（离线子集）准确率与成本对比

OSWorld 2.1 衡量代理操作真实计算机完成长时间、多步骤任务的能力。

在早期测试中，我们的客户报告的结果与上述性能和成本改进一致。以下是他们对该新模型的评价：

引述

“我们对 Claude Haiku 5.5 印象非常深刻，尤其是它的速度。我们在 AI Teammates（我们的人工智能代理产品）的评估套件中运行了它，涵盖了对缺陷进行分类、设置项目以及搜索大型项目组合以发现高风险或逾期工作等用例。与我们目前使用的模型相比，任务完成的延迟降低了 30% 以上，每个代理轮次的推理速度最高提升了 2.5 倍。体验明显更加流畅。”

公司Asana

作者Aaron Vinh，资深软件工程师

定价

下表展示了 Claude Haiku 5.5 的定价与我们其他模型的对比。当用于提示词不超过 100,000 个 token 的任务时，Haiku 5.5 的性价比尤为突出，而此类任务约占我们此前 Haiku 模型请求量的 90%。

每 100 万 token 价格	Haiku 5.5
提示词不超过 / 超过 100k	Haiku 4.5	Sonnet 5.5
缓存读取	$0.01 / $0.05	$0.10	$0.10
缓存写入	$0.125 / $0.625	$1.25	$2.50
输入 token	$0.10 / $0.50	$1.00	$2.00
输出 token	$0.50 / $2.50	$5.00	$10.00
安全性

对齐。相较于 Haiku 4.5，Claude Haiku 5.5 在几乎所有对齐评估中都展现出重大改进。特别是，我们发现其行为失准的实例大幅减少，配合滥用的意愿也更低。该模型的系统卡更详细地描述了我们的评估流程和结果。

保障措施。与其能力相符，Haiku 5.5 的网络安全保障措施比 Haiku 4.5 更为严格，但比我们应用于其他近期模型的措施略为宽松。在网络安全方面，相比我们对 Sonnet 5.5 的保障措施，它们允许更广泛的防御性任务，但仍会阻止渗透测试及其他更可能被攻击者使用的技术。

Haiku 5.5 的生物学保障措施与 Sonnet 5、Sonnet 5.5 和 Opus 5 相同。它们允许研究性生物学问题，但会限制访问我们判断可能造成危害的请求。从事更广泛生物学和网络活动的组织可以申请我们的生命科学验证计划和网络验证计划。

可用性

Claude Haiku 5.5 现已在所有平台上线，包括 Amazon Web Services、Google Cloud 和 Microsoft Azure。在 Claude 平台上，开发者可以通过 claude-haiku-5-5 开始使用。

详情请参阅我们的迁移指南。

更多更新

除了 Claude Haiku 5.5 的新定价外，我们还在进一步提升模型和产品的价值。

首先，从今天起，我们将降低 Claude Sonnet 5.5 的缓存读取价格。缓存读取现在便宜 50%：每百万 token 0.10 美元，而非 0.20 美元。由于缓存读取占模型 token 消耗的很大一部分，这将使 Sonnet 5.5 在大多数智能体任务上的成本降低约 20%。

例如，以下是此次降价对 Sonnet 5.5 在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上性能与成本之比的影响：

Terminal-Bench 4.0准确率与成本对比

Terminal-Bench 4.0 衡量模型在命令行界面内完成复杂、多步骤专业任务的能力。

这张图表说明了 Haiku 5.5 与我们更大模型之间的一个重要区别。对于像 Terminal-Bench 4.0 所衡量的复杂智能体编码任务，Sonnet 5.5 和 Opus 5.5 仍是更好的选择。相比之下，Haiku 5.5 最适合范围更窄的任务——这些任务若使用此前版本的 Claude 可能会因成本过高而无法实现——例如压缩、摘要或子智能体工作。

其次，本周我们将向所有 Max 和 Team 订阅用户推出每月 API 额度，可用于 Claude 平台。Max 5x 用户每月将获得 100 美元额度，Max 20x 用户将获得 200 美元，Team 订阅用户将获得最高 500 美元，并在其用户之间共享。这些额度旨在让我们的用户能够尝试构建调用我们 API 的工具、应用和智能体。它们可用于我们的任何模型。如需了解更多信息，请参阅我们的帮助中心文章。

对于开发者，我们还更新了 Claude Python 和 TypeScript SDK，以测试版形式新增对 computer use 和 browser use 的支持。鉴于 Haiku 5.5 在速度、能力和价格方面的综合优势，它尤其适合这些任务。你可以在我们的 Claude 平台文档中了解更多相关信息。

Want Employees to Embrace AI? Stop Selling It as a Productivity Tool

AI 导读

Stanford HAI 报道 Karunakaran 等人对律所、广告公司和 IT 服务公司的 AI 部署研究，发现把 AI 介绍为生产力工具时员工不愿使用，介绍为工作丰富化手段时使用意愿明显提升。在一家律所的对照观察中，以丰富工作为目标引入 AI 工具 LawBot 的部门，使用量比强调提效的部门高 58%，尝试新用法多 70%。研究还强调配套培训、探索时间和调整考核指标的重要性。

想让员工拥抱 AI？别再把它当作生产力工具来推销

日期

2026年10月7日

主题

劳动力、劳工生成式 AI教育、技能

管理者如何引入和支持 AI，决定了员工是接纳还是抵制这项技术。

生成式 AI 工具的采用速度很快。2023 年，全球 55% 的组织报告使用了 AI。两年后，这一数字达到了 88%。然而，尽管增长如此迅速——且代表着可观的投入——员工对这项技术的反馈却褒贬不一。

“这些工具在向员工推出时如何被框定，是这件事的重要一环，”斯坦福大学工程学院助理教授、斯坦福以人为本人工智能研究院（HAI）教职附属成员Arvind Karunakaran 说。“更重要的是，管理者是否会兑现他们所做的承诺。如果他们说 AI 是为了丰富工作，那么他们是否投入资源让这一点成真？”

Karunakaran 与弗吉尼亚大学的 Roshni Raveendhran 以及达特茅斯学院的 Tami Kim 一起，研究了一家律师事务所、一家广告公司和一家 IT 服务公司的 AI 部署情况，以更好地理解是什么推动了员工的采用。他们发现了一个一致的模式：当 AI 被框定为生产力工具时，员工往往不愿使用它。然而，当它被呈现为一种丰富工作的方式时，员工就有动力去探索如何最好地使用它——前提是他们有时间和机会去探索。

让工作更有意义，而不仅仅是更高效

研究人员开展了两项职场研究。在第一项研究中，他们采访了三家已采用生成式 AI 工具公司的 184 名员工。在行政、创意和技术岗位上，被要求使用 AI 的员工表示，他们感觉自己的工作被剥夺了意义。这种丧失反过来又削弱了他们学习新技能的动力。“我不太愿意学习与工作相关的新技能，”一位员工解释道，“因为感觉我今天学到的东西下个月就会过时。”

最有说服力的证据来自第二项研究，在该研究中，团队在一家律师事务所花了近两年时间观察两个部门，这两个部门在业务领域、规模以及薪酬和晋升结构上几乎完全相同。管理人员为两组人员授予了同一款AI工具的全公司许可——研究人员将其称为“LawBot”——旨在帮助起草合同和保密协议。两个部门之间的关键区别在于管理者如何引入这一工具。

在第一个部门，管理者向律师助理推销LawBot，称其可以更快地起草文件并缩短周转时间。使用该工具后，律师助理们表示感觉自己“只是机器上的又一个齿轮”，并且只将其用于现有任务，而非探索新的应用。

在第二个部门，管理者问律师助理：你们觉得哪些任务最无聊，有哪些事情你们一直想做却从未有时间去做？LawBot能否帮助处理日常任务，腾出时间做更有趣的工作？在获得时间自由探索LawBot后，律师助理们开始将其用于法律研究和案件分析，交流哪些方法行之有效的技巧，并争取参加与律师的法律策略会议。该部门的律师助理使用LawBot的频率比其他部门的同事高出58%，尝试探索的次数高出70%。

“当引入AI工具时，管理者往往痴迷于生产率的提升，”卡鲁纳卡兰说。“但如果你不同时努力回答人们的工作将如何改善或变得更加丰富，这一举措很可能会适得其反。”

管理者如何界定引入AI的理由对其成功部署起着决定性作用，但这并非唯一因素。第二个部门的管理者为律师助理提供了LawBot的正式培训、每周的知识分享午餐、与供应商的问答环节，以及针对更复杂任务（如法律研究）的非正式指导。此外，每周还留出时间让律师助理自行探索和了解该工具。

“你需要搭建这种脚手架，让承诺显得可信，”卡鲁纳卡兰说。“否则，员工会认为这不过是空话。”

衡量价值，而非数量

随着AI重塑工作职责，员工的评估方式也必须改变。卡鲁纳卡兰指出，律师助理传统上以其年度或季度案件量来评判。

“但这并不是他们利用AI从事新型工作的正确指标，”他说。利用该技术进行深入法律研究和案件分析的律师助理产出了高价值的工作，但这也更耗时，意味着他们承接的案件更少。“因此，指标需要重新调整，以适应新的岗位概况和任务组合。”

错误的指标还可能引发适得其反的行为。一些公司追踪员工的AI令牌消耗量，或处理或生成的文本量，并将大量使用等同于价值。但这一策略鼓励员工为使用AI而使用AI——用卡鲁纳卡兰的话说，就是生成猫咪表情包来达到配额——而非将其用于正当的商业目标。

最适合AI的工作

促成AI成功采用的另一个因素是某一特定工作由强捆绑任务还是弱捆绑任务组成。

例如，销售岗位由紧密捆绑的任务组成，如研究客户、建立关系、谈判和达成交易。“你不能随意地拆解和重新捆绑这些任务，”Karunakaran 说。公司可能会部署 AI 进行客户研究，但销售人员仍全程参与其中。“销售人员仍然需要了解客户，并亲自在场达成交易，所以这是一个强捆绑型的工作。”

相反，由弱捆绑任务组成的工作——例如律师助理工作或医疗转录，其中包含与文档管理相关的各种不同任务——可能更容易受到 AI 自动化的影响，但其模块化特性使采用变得容易得多。

无论 AI 部署的范围有多广、速度有多快，它在工作场所的成功与否，与其说取决于技术本身，不如说取决于部署它的理由、用于反映真实价值的指标，以及给予员工以有意义的方式去尝试和接触它的时间和资源。

“尽管 AI 的承诺是它会处理日常任务，让人们腾出时间从事更高层次的工作，但经常发生的情况是，管理者看到节省下来的时间，就提高了对人们应该完成多少同样的工作的期望，”Karunakaran 说。“如果管理者希望 AI 丰富人们的工作并创造组织价值，他们就必须为员工创造空间去学习、承担新责任，并因其贡献的价值而得到认可和奖励。要实现这种可能性，需要致力于培养人才，同时致力于适应技术。”

LlamaIndex 发布 OpenDocRouter：一个 API 统一调用多种文档解析模型

Introducing OpenDocRouter: every document model under one API

AI 导读

LlamaIndex 推出 OpenDocRouter 平台，通过统一 API 将文档（PDF、PNG、JPEG 或 URL）解析为 markdown，接入 Claude Opus 5.5、Gemini 3 Flash、GPT-6 Luna 等 5 个前沿模型和 MinerU2.5-Pro、PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 等 5 个开源模型。

正文 · AI 翻译
中文
原文

OCR 模型非常多，而且每周都有更多新模型发布。在 HuggingFace 上快速搜索“ocr”就能看到成千上万个已发布的模型。此外，前沿实验室几乎每个月都在推出新的模型，这些模型也能很好地读取文档（尽管有时价格不菲）。使用这些模型进行文档解析通常都需要同样的几个步骤：设计提示词（如果适用）、处理速率限制、管理部署及相关成本，并在新模型发布时对其进行基准测试。

这正是我们 LlamaIndex 特别擅长的事情，今天我们推出 OpenDocRouter，以此分享这项工作。

什么是 OpenDocRouter？

OpenDocRouter 是一个使用最新开源和前沿模型进行文档 → markdown 解析的平台。每个模型都运行一套版本化的配方，包含提示词、处理和设置。使用该 API 非常简单：

Shell
复制
curl https://https://www.opendocrouter.ai/v1/parse \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "opendatalab/mineru2.5-pro",
    "document": { "url": "https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762" },
    "layout": true
  }'

该 API 接受 PDF、PNG、JPEG 或指向这些文件格式的 URL。该 API 允许你在同步响应（直接返回结果）和异步响应（创建一个需要轮询的任务）之间切换。同步响应最多支持 50 页。请求可以处理最多 500 页或 50MB 的输入。

每个模型都在 ParseBench 上从质量和成本两方面进行基准测试。在发布时，我们选择了一组覆盖我们基准测试各个角落的模型：

前沿模型：Claude Opus 5.5、Gemini 3 Flash、Gemini 3.8 Flash、GPT-5.6 Terra、GPT-6 Luna。
开源模型：Infinity-Parser2-Flash、MinerU2.5-Pro、TeleOCR、dots.mocr、PaddleOCR-VL-1.6

边界框与布局

每个模型对边界框和布局的保证各不相同。有些模型原生输出边界框，有些需要提示词，还有些完全做不到。

为了弥补这一差距，我们构建了一个可以应用于任何模型的定位引擎。在请求中设置 layout: True，即可生成带有定位边界框和按阅读顺序排列的布局元素的 markdown。这也意味着所有模型都会产生相同的布局类别：title、section_header、text、list_item、table、picture、chart、formula、caption、footnote、page_header、page_footer、code、form、key_value。

定价

OpenDocRouter 推出时采用纯基于 token 的计费方式，相当简单直接。创建账户，从 25 美元起充值额度，然后开始解析。启用布局会增加每百万 token 0.2 美元的费用，如果处理过程中任何页面失败，则不会收费。

截至 2026 年 10 月 7 日，我们的定价如下：

模型	输入（$/1M）	缓存输入（$/1M）	输出（$/1M）	每 1k 页成本（ParseBench）
Claude Opus 5.5	$4.00	$0.20	$20.00	$48.82
Gemini 3 Flash	$0.50	$0.05	$3.00	$19.67
Gemini 3.8 Flash	$0.75	$0.08	$3.75	$5.91
GPT-5.6 Terra	$2.00	$0.20	$12.00	$19.89
GPT-6 Luna	$0.10	$0.01	$0.50	$0.80
Infinity-Parser2-Flash	$0.24	-	$1.16	$4.34
MinerU2.5-Pro	$0.08	-	$0.39	$0.86
TeleOCR	$0.25	-	$1.22	$2.70
dots.mocr	$0.31	-	$1.53	$3.97
PaddleOCR-VL-1.6	$0.24	-	$1.20	$2.17
添加新模型

当我们可以提供的新模型发布时，我们有相应的流程可以快速将它们添加到 OpenDocRouter。我们会让它们通过 ParseBench 运行，并以此校准提示词、成本和其他设置，从而尽可能提供最佳用户体验。

我们还计划持续改进最受欢迎的模型：无论是通过更好的提示词、更好的托管以降低延迟，还是更多其他方面。

OpenDocRouter 与 LlamaParse 对比

我们将 OpenDocRouter 视为一个平台，用于快速托管最新模型，同时让开发者能够轻松在现有模型之间切换和路由，并且只为实际使用量付费。该 API 本身易于使用，同时提供对模型的广泛访问。

LlamaParse 是我们的托管文档平台。它内置了手工调优的解析层级、企业级管控、自托管部署，以及模式提取和索引等其他 API。

立即试用 OpenDocRouter

OpenDocRouter 现已上线，可供试用。浏览模型和文档，注册并生成 API 密钥，今天就解析你的文档。

Sierra 与 Meta 联合多家企业发布 Personal Agent Protocol 开放协议

Introducing Personal Agent Protocol

AI 导读

Sierra 与 Meta 联合 Genesys、Instinct、Rocket、Shopify、Stripe、Walmart 等伙伴宣布开发 Personal Agent Protocol，一个定义个人 AI 智能体如何与企业交互的开放标准，任何人都可实现。

正文 · AI 翻译
中文
原文

个人 AI 代理正在席卷全球。人们用它们做各种事情，从安排预约到预订航班，再到购买汽车保险。AI 改变消费者行为的速度之快，以及我们中有多少人在使用个人代理时经历那些令人难以置信的“等等，它刚刚做到了”的时刻，都非同寻常。毫不意外，企业正在询问，他们如何才能最好地尊重消费者的选择，同时保护他们的隐私和安全。

因此，今天我们很高兴地宣布 Personal Agent Protocol——这是 Meta 和 Sierra 与 Genesys、Instinct、Rocket、Shopify、Stripe 和 Walmart 等行业伙伴共同开发的一项开放标准，它定义了个人代理如何与企业互动。我们设计它是为了处理身份验证，赋能消费者，并让企业了解个人代理通过其网站、API 或公司代理做了什么。它开放给任何人实施。

需要解决的问题

如今，大多数个人代理像人一样使用网站和应用程序——加载页面并点击表单。当这样无法完成任务时，它们可能会拨打公司的支持热线或打开其网络聊天。这可能耗时很长，而且代理可能无法完成任务。但直接连接可以在几秒钟内安全地完成同样的任务。

要大规模采用，这种连接必须对各方都有效。每个人都想要安全，但他们也有不同的需求：

消费者想要速度、可靠性和信任——希望任务第一次就能由他们可以信赖、会为其最大利益行事的个人代理正确完成。
品牌想要可见性和控制权——希望知道个人代理何时代表客户行事，并自行决定它可以做什么。
构建个人代理的公司想要效率和访问权——希望有一种直接、一致的方式与参与的公司合作。
工作原理

我们正在构建的 Personal Agent Protocol 背后的原则是，消费者决定给予其个人代理什么访问权限，公司则为这些代理可以做什么设定参数。它使公司能够以对客户最有利的方式与个人代理合作：通过其现有网站和 API，或通过自己的代理。

Personal Agent Protocol 从网站开始，个人代理可以在那里发现公司提供什么以及如何联系它。然后，个人代理代表其用户开始一个会话。它可以以访客身份开始，这可能足以检查产品可用性或询问退货政策。当任务需要访问客户账户时，他们可以在公司页面上登录，或使用他们已经在其个人代理上设置的凭据。客户始终掌控一切，决定代理拥有只读还是写入权限。

该会话基于 OAuth 构建，这是一种用于授权访问的成熟标准。它跨渠道延续，因此登录前提出的问题和登录后进行的订单更改属于同一次访问。在此基础上，个人代理可以使用公司认为能提供最佳客户体验的任何途径来完成任务：

其网站：浏览公司的常规网页。
其 API：通过基于 MCP 和 OpenAPI 等标准构建的接口进行连接。
其代理：处理需要对话的任务，例如保修索赔。

公司决定提供什么，个人智能体获得一致的连接方式，客户则获得更快的办事途径。

下一步计划

我们希望与正在使用该协议的公司和个人智能体开发者共同完善它，也很高兴 Instinct 也将加入这一努力。我们欢迎所有合作伙伴，并计划于本月晚些时候发布 v0.1 规范，与感兴趣的相关方举办设计研讨会，并发布参考实现以帮助开发者上手。

更精细的权限设置可以让客户和公司对具体操作设定限制。推送通知可以让公司在航班延误或订单发货的那一刻告知个人智能体。支付扩展可以让个人智能体在不共享信用卡信息的情况下完成购买。

随着个人智能体承担我们越来越多的日常任务，公司需要清晰、安全的方式与它们协作，同时继续提供值得信赖的体验。Personal Agent Protocol 为他们提供了这一基础——让公司和个人智能体能够为他们共同的客户把事情办成。

亚利桑那州法院裁定AI生成受害者视频带有不当情感分量，凶手须重新量刑

Her AI-Generated Video Swayed the Judge. The Court Said it Carried 'Undue Emotional Weight'

AI 导读

亚利桑那州上诉法院裁定，Gabriel Horcasitas过失杀人案量刑中使用的受害者Christopher Pelkey AI生成视频带有不当情感重量，罪名维持但刑期须重新考虑。

另有 1 家信源报道
正文 · AI 翻译
中文
原文

亚利桑那州一名被判过失杀人罪的男子将获得重新量刑，因为一段由AI生成的、让受害者在坟墓之外开口说话的视频被裁定作为影响陈述带有“过度的情感分量”。亚利桑那州一家上诉法院裁定，过失杀人罪的指控维持不变，但法官必须因AI而重新考虑该男子的刑期长短。

2021年，Gabriel Horcasitas在一起路怒事件中开枪打死了Christopher Pelkey。陪审团裁定他过失杀人罪成立。在Horcasitas的量刑听证会上，Pelkey的姐姐Stacey Wales在受害者影响陈述中播放了一段AI生成的视频，视频中是她弟弟的形象。在这段视频中，她用自己撰写的文字让AI生成的Pelkey形象说出这些话，AI版Pelkey原谅了杀害他的人，并说他们在另一世“本可以成为朋友”。 

“我很喜欢那段视频，”法官在宣判10年半最高刑期时说道。

Wales告诉404 Media，她制作这段视频的意图是影响法官。“这不正是你希望人与人之间的联结所成为的样子吗？”她说。“你有没有过看完一部电影出来说：‘嗯，那太煽情了。那太有冲击力了。’人与人之间的联结是有力量的，而试图把这种联结传达给一个从未认识过另一个人、从未认识过地球上这个人的对象，把这个人37年的一生浓缩到一场两小时的量刑活动中，是很难做到的，我认为受害者和受害者家属应该被给予一切机会。”

量刑之后，Horcasitas提出上诉。他主张，AI版Pelkey的视频不可采纳，因为它带有“过度的情感分量”，而且根据404 Media查阅的法庭文件，这段“对受害者的逼真AI再现传达出一种权威性和真实性”，对法官产生了“心理冲击”。

上诉法院同意这一主张，并援引了State v. Rose案——2007年的一起谋杀案，一名男子因谋杀一名警察被判处死刑。在该案量刑的受害者影响环节中，法官看到了那名警察的孩子们在其墓旁的几张照片。法院称，那些照片几乎越界，足以使法官产生偏见。

“这段AI视频越过了那条线。与Rose案中的照片不同——那些照片捕捉的是年幼幸存受害者尤为痛切的一刻——这里的AI视频[...]并不反映真实事件，”法庭文件称。

“它显然影响了量刑法官，这位法官说他‘很喜欢那段视频’，并觉得它‘是真实的’，并指出AI受害者对Horcacistas‘显而易见的宽恕’，”法庭文件称。“基于这一记录，法官对AI视频的考量使Horcasitas受到了如此严重的偏见，以致量刑程序从根本上变得不公正。”

Wales和Pelkey的其他家人过去五年来因他的死亡而频繁出入各个法庭。如果当前裁决维持不变，她将从纽约前往亚利桑那州，通过她弟弟AI生成的口说出与第一次相同的陈述，只是不再有那段AI生成的视频。当初说“我很喜欢那段视频”的那位同一位法官将进行量刑。

“很可能，同样的人会再次下去发表他们的陈述，而我会再次宣读我第一次为自己写的受害者影响陈述，我也会再次表达 Chris 的 AI 脚本情感，”她说。“如果我需要亲自站在那里宣读，这在法律上是合法的，我已准备好这样做。Chris 的情感不会改变。传达方式会变。”

Wales 说，AI 版本中她哥哥说出的话是她写的，并非 AI 生成。她还指出，审判期间只有法官、她的家人和 Horcacistas 家人看过它。“这并未作为证据提供。陪审团从未看到过这个，”她说。“这只是在判决确定、有罪判决之后才创建的。”

她还指出，AI 视频只是当天提供的更大证词的一部分。“我认为[法官]被一段声音片段不公平地代表了，”她说。据 Wales 说，法官讲了大约半小时，只提到过一次 AI 视频。Wales 自己将法官说他喜欢 AI 生成的影响陈述的声音片段上传到 YouTube，并在那里疯传。

但她也表示，她理解 AI 是一项新技术，当她播放 AI 生成的她哥哥的视频时，她正在做别人尚未做过的事。她将其比作 19 世纪末法院对摄影的看法。 

“大约花了 15 年[...]以及大约 五个里程碑案件 在美国一直上诉到最高法院，摄影才成为法庭上用于证据、识别和证词等的公认标准，”她说。“我相信这就是我们现在在 AI 上看到的情况。它是一种全新的媒介。”

Wales 说，她明白自己正在开创先例，无论好坏，她都接受。“总会有第一个案例，所以这份责任压在我身上，我需要小心如何为此辩护，如何解释其推动力、目标、动机以及所创建内容的真实性，因为有受害者未来依赖言论自由，我确实相信受害者和他们的家人应该拥有一切可用机会来表达他们的观点，”她说。

新的量刑没有确定日期。“我们确实尊重法院的意见，如果我们需要在这些限制内运作，我已准备好宣读 Chris 的 AI 版本第一次宣读的同一份脚本，”她说。“他的情感没有改变。我们对他会如何看待整件事的看法没有改变。我作为 Chris 的想象观点所写的文字仍然没有改变，也不会改变。”
